title: FIRST RECORDS OF HUMPBACK WHALES INCLUDING CALVES AT GOLFO DULCE AND ISLA DEL COCO, COSTA RICA, SUGGESTING GEOGRAPHICAL OVERLAP OF NORTHERN AND SOUTHERN HEMISPHERE POPULATIONS
summary: The original published record establishing that Golfo Dulce is used by humpback whales from both the Northern and Southern Hemisphere breeding stocks — the observation on which every later statement about the gulf's unusual dual-hemisphere whale use rests. Acevedo and Smultea reported the first sightings of humpbacks, including cow-calf pairs, inside Golfo Dulce and at Isla del Coco, and argued that the presence of animals in both boreal and austral winter seasons implies geographical overlap of two otherwise separate populations. This is the anchor citation for the claim, repeated in the reference lists of essentially all subsequent Golfo Dulce cetacean work (Oviedo et al. 2015, Bessesen 2015).
verbatim_finding: FIRST RECORDS OF HUMPBACK WHALES INCLUDING CALVES AT GOLFO DULCE AND ISLA DEL COCO, COSTA RICA, SUGGESTING GEOGRAPHICAL OVERLAP OF NORTHERN AND SOUTHERN HEMISPHERE POPULATIONS
data_availability: None available to us: Wiley serves neither abstract nor full text without a subscription, and Crossref holds no deposited abstract. Sighting records are described in the paper text only.
caveat: Publisher blocked retrieval (HTTP 403) and no abstract is deposited in Crossref or Semantic Scholar, so the only verbatim text we could confirm is the published title as registered with Crossref. The dual-hemisphere claim itself should be read through the better-documented Rasmussen et al. 2007 record. Small sample: a handful of sightings from the early 1990s.

title: A snapshot view of some vertical distributions of water parameters at a deep (200 m) station in the fjord-like Golfo Dulce, embayment, Costa Rica
summary: Eight field trips between June 1993 and September 1995 profiling temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen and inorganic nutrients at 10 m intervals down the 200 m station. Its value is as a counterweight to the 'permanently anoxic' shorthand: across this whole period deep oxygen was low (3.00–0.20 mg/L) but never actually anoxic. It also resolves the physical structure — thermocline between 25 and 60 m, halocline near 40 m, a 34-salinity layer over a thick 35-salinity bottom layer — and attributes the nutrient-rich bottom water to sporadic ocean inflow over the 60 m sill. The vertical nitrite structure led the authors to infer anammox independently.
verbatim_finding: from 60 m depth down to the bottom (200 m), dissolved oxygen concentrations were low during the whole study, ranging from 3.00 mg/L to 0.20 mg/L, although anoxic conditions were not detected.
data_availability: Profiles for each of the eight cruises are given as figures and tables in the article. Underlying Niskin-bottle data held at CIMAR-UCR; not deposited.
caveat: Single station, eight occupations — explicitly a 'snapshot'. Its non-detection of anoxia over 1993–1995 sits in tension with contemporaneous reports of anoxia and H2S, which is itself the point: the deep layer is variable.

title: Coverage and Distribution of the Mangrove Species in the Térraba-Sierpe National Wetland, Costa Rica
container: Anuário do Instituto de Geociências - UFRJ
summary: Remote-sensing mapping of Costa Rica's largest mangrove system, the Ramsar-listed Térraba-Sierpe National Wetland immediately north of the Osa Peninsula, using a 2012 RapidEye spectral classification over roughly 14 800 ha. It resolves the spatial distribution of the dominant taxa — Rhizophora racemosa, Pelliciera rhizophorae, mixed R. racemosa/P. rhizophorae association, Rhizophora mangle and the fern Acrostichum aureum — and links their arrangement to geomorphology and to land-use change in the adjacent catchments. This is the regional counterweight to the small Golfo Dulce stands: the same species pool, an order of magnitude more area, and a delta-driven rather than embayment-driven setting.
verbatim_finding: El Humedal Nacional Térraba-Sierpe se localiza el sureste de Costa Rica, tiene una extensión aproximada de 14800 ha de mangle
data_availability: Species-level classification derived from a 2012 RapidEye scene; classified maps and area figures are published in the open-access PDF, source imagery is commercial.
caveat: Single-date classification with no reported independent accuracy assessment in the abstract; the Crossref-registered title is English while the article itself is published in Spanish under the title 'Cobertura y Distribución de las Especies de Mangle en el Humedal Nacional Térraba-Sierpe, Costa Rica'.

title: En defensa del golfo Dulce y por los intereses comunales y nacionales
summary: The clearest published account of the civil-society coalition that actually contests development decisions in the gulf, written by the executive director of Fundación Neotrópica. It describes the alliance between the Frente Nacional por la Protección de los Humedales and the Frente por el Golfo Dulce — a mix of local community organisations and leaders on the Osa Peninsula — and the combined strategy of public awareness work, technical fora and litigation aimed at protecting an Osa development model built around its protected areas. For collaborator mapping this is the single most useful item in the harvest: it names the organised actors and the person leading one of them.
verbatim_finding: el Frente Nacional por la Protección de los Humedales (al que pertenece Fundación Neotrópica) se ha unido con el Frente por el Golfo Dulce (compuesto por una mezcla de organizaciones y líderes comunales de base local en la península de Osa)
data_availability: None; a position piece citing the author's own economic-valuation work on the Osa Peninsula.
caveat: Explicitly an advocacy statement by a party to the dispute; useful as evidence of who is organised and around what, not as neutral assessment.

title: Allen Coral Atlas satellite-derived bathymetry and habitat mapping methods
authors: Arizona State University Center for Global Discovery and Conservation Science
summary: The realistic ceiling on satellite-derived bathymetry for this gulf, and a useful check on optimism about filling the gap from space. The Atlas produces 10 m bathymetry from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance, using a 12-month median composite chosen for minimal cloud and turbid water, with geomorphic mapping to about 15 m depth and benthic mapping to about 10 m. Golfo Dulce receives more than 4.5 m of rain a year through four rivers and carries surface plumes that drop salinity below 30 over a third of its area, so the optically shallow window the method needs is exactly what the gulf lacks. Satellite methods can address the reef margins; they cannot see the 215 m basin.
verbatim_finding: The bathymetry maps are created at a resolution of 10 m using the Google Earth Engine (GEE) Sentinel-2 surface reflectance dataset.
data_availability: Bathymetry, geomorphic and benthic layers downloadable as GeoTIFF (16-bit integer, depth in centimetres) after free registration, for mapped coral reef areas between roughly 30°N and 30°S.
caveat: Methods page is undated, so year is recorded as null. Coverage of the Golfo Dulce margins specifically was not verified layer-by-layer in this harvest; the entry documents the method's depth and turbidity limits, which is the point that matters here.

title: Modernos "fan deltas" en la Bahía de Golfito, Costa Rica
summary: A small but directly relevant Spanish-language study of active sediment delivery into Golfo Dulce itself. Ten small fan deltas are described along roughly 7 km of the NW–SE coast of Bahía de Golfito, built by short, steep streams draining a fault-controlled mountain front that runs parallel to the shore. Alvarado reads them as a geomorphic signal of ongoing uplift of the Osa Peninsula combined with progressive infilling of the bay, and notes the climate (very high rainfall) and tidal regime as enabling conditions. Also summarises the local basement: basaltic breccias with calcareous and siliceous pelagic sediments, interpreted by Obando (1986) as an ophiolitic complex of at least Cretaceous age, intruded by doleritic dykes now uplifted into the coastal mountain front.
verbatim_finding: Ellos son una evidencia del reciente levantamiento de la Península de Osa y el paulatino relleno de la Bahía.
data_availability: Morphological and sedimentological descriptions and a location map of the ten fan deltas. Scanned PDF freely downloadable from the UCR archive; no dataset.
caveat: Descriptive and local in scope (Bahía de Golfito only); no dating or quantified sedimentation rates. Scanned PDF, no text layer.

title: Ecosistemas coralinos del Área de Conservación Osa, Costa Rica: estructura y necesidades de conservación
summary: A standardised re-survey (2013–2014) of 27 sites across five localities of the Osa Conservation Area, including Golfo Dulce, measuring substrate cover, rugosity, macroinvertebrate density and reef-fish biomass. It demonstrates that reefs do persist inside this fjord-like, sediment-loaded basin: turf dominates (62.7 %) and live coral cover is moderate overall (16.5 %), but Golfo Dulce and Caño Island reefs showed significant coral-cover recovery since previous surveys, and Golfo Dulce held the highest macroinvertebrate diversity and density of any locality. Its reef-fish composition also differs from the rest of ACOSA — the inner-gulf reef community is genuinely distinct, not merely a depauperate version of the open-coast one.
verbatim_finding: Golfo Dulce presented the highest diversity and density of macroinvertebrates and significant differences were observed between localities.
data_availability: Transect-level cover, rugosity, invertebrate density and fish biomass data summarised per site and locality in the open-access article; a baseline for most sites is published here for the first time.
caveat: Two-year snapshot; the reported recovery is relative to heterogeneous earlier studies with different methods, so the trend is suggestive rather than a monitored time series.

title: El potencial arqueológico del Golfo Dulce, Pacífico Sur de Costa Rica, investigación - acción: Zona de Playa Cacao El Sitio Alto Purruja Cat. UCR N° 455
container: Universidad de Costa Rica, Facultad de Ciencias Sociales, Escuela de Antropología
summary: The only monograph located that treats the archaeology of the Golfo Dulce shoreline itself rather than the Diquís Delta or the Osa interior. It is an action-research study centred on Playa Cacao — directly across the bay from Golfito — and the Alto Purruja site, framed under 'arqueología social' with community participation. It matters here because it establishes that the gulf margin holds a recorded, catalogued archaeological potential (UCR catalogue no. 455) independent of the World Heritage sites inland, and it is the natural starting point for anyone reconstructing pre-Columbian use of the gulf's own coast.
verbatim_finding: El potencial arqueológico del Golfo Dulce, Pacífico Sur de Costa Rica, investigación - acción : Zona de Playa Cacao El Sitio Alto Purruja Cat. UCR N° 455
data_availability: No digital copy located. Holdings are recorded in the SIIDCA-CSUCA union catalogue against the Sistema de Bibliotecas de la Universidad de Costa Rica; consultation requires a UCR library request. Subject headings: ARQUEOLOGIA COSTARRICENSE > INVESTIGACIONES > GOLFO DULCE; ARQUEOLOGIA SOCIAL > GOLFO DULCE.
caveat: Only the catalogue record was retrieved, not the text — no abstract is published, so the scope described here is inferred from the title and subject headings. Sebastian should decide whether a UCR request is worth making; this is the highest-value unretrieved item in the topic.

title: Caracterización acústica de fincas bajo pago por servicios ambientales en la Reserva Forestal Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: A rare empirical test of whether Costa Rica's flagship conservation instrument — payment for environmental services on private land — is actually delivering inside the Golfo Dulce catchment. Soundscapes were recorded at eleven Osa Peninsula sites, nine on PSA-enrolled private farms and two inside Corcovado, and six acoustic indices plus automated detection of two indicator bird species were compared. The uncomfortable result is that acoustic indices did not discriminate ecosystem quality between farms, with the most fragmented sites showing the highest acoustic activity and diversity through edge effects; species-level vocalisation detection was more promising. Relevant because PSA is the main mechanism SINAC has for influencing land use in the Reserva Forestal Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: In Costa Rica, the payment for environmental services (PSA) represents a mechanism to protect forests on private farms, but it lacks specific indicators on the state of biodiversity and forest conservation.
data_availability: Acoustic index values per site and automated detection results are reported in the open-access article; the raw recordings from 25 May - 1 June 2021 are not deposited with the paper.
caveat: Eight days of recording at eleven sites — a small, short survey. The quoted line is from the journal's own English abstract of a Spanish-language article.

title: Gas seeps on the margins of the Golfo Dulce pull-apart basin, southern Costa Rica
summary: The clearest published statement of the mechanism that answers the central puzzle — how a fjord-shaped basin exists in the tropics without glaciers. Berrangé places Golfo Dulce in a braided system of NW-trending dextral wrench faults that are the onshore continuation of the Panamá–Coiba Fracture Zone, and argues the gulf is a modern strike-slip pull-apart basin, with the flanking Osa and Burica Peninsulas as tilted mini-horsts. He explicitly draws the analogy to Crowell's model for the Gulf of California and Baja California. The paper's nominal subject is four onshore gas seeps on Osa and Burica, which he interprets in the context of this tectonic setting.
verbatim_finding: Golfo Dulce and Golfo de Chiriquí are modern pull-apart basins, whereas the adjacent Osa Peninsula, Fila Golfito and the Burica Peninsula are mini-horsts with a gentle (2-5°) NE tilt.
data_availability: Gas composition analyses from two Costa Rican seep localities are tabulated in the note. No separate dataset. Scanned PDF is free to download from the UCR journal archive.
caveat: Published as a Nota Científica (short note), not a full research paper. The scanned PDF has no text layer. The pull-apart interpretation is directly disputed by Kriz (1990).

title: The Osa Group: an auriferous Pliocene sedimentary unit from the Osa Peninsula, southern Costa Rica
summary: Defines the Osa Group, the Mid–Upper Pliocene clastic sequence (conglomerates, sandstones, siltstones, claystones) that sits unconformably on Nicoya Complex basement and is itself overlain unconformably by Quaternary sediments of the Puerto Jiménez Group. It supersedes the older Charco Azul and Armuelles Formation nomenclature on Osa. For the basin-formation question this is the key stratigraphic evidence: the Pliocene sediments accumulated in intermittently subsiding pull-apart basins governed by wrench faulting, in a tectonic geometry the author argues is still operating today, with Golfo Dulce itself as the modern equivalent. Also documents that the region's placer gold is concentrated in the conglomeratic members near the basal unconformity.
verbatim_finding: Within this tectonic setting the Golfo Dulce basin and the Coto Colorado-Chiriquí lowlands form pull-apart or tipped-wedge basins, whereas the Osa and the Burica Peninsula, and the offshore Coiba Ridge, are tilted horst blocks.
data_availability: Stratigraphic sections, micropalaeontological age determinations and lithological logs are reproduced in the paper. Scanned PDF freely downloadable from the UCR archive; no machine-readable data.
caveat: Scanned image PDF, no text layer. Crossref records the deposit year (2011) rather than the printed issue year (1989) given here.

title: Gold from the Golfo Dulce placer province, southern Costa Rica
summary: Traces the region's gold back to its source rock and in doing so characterises the basement the gulf is cut into. The 'source beds' are shown to lie within the Nicoya Complex here — an obducted segment of ophiolitic oceanic crust of E-MORB type enriched in large-ion-lithophile elements, which Berrangé interprets as back-arc basin crust analogous to the Mariana Trough. Gold was first concentrated in epithermal quartz lodes during Late Cretaceous–Early Tertiary submarine volcanism, then released by obduction, isostatic uplift and erosion into eluvial, colluvial and alluvial placers in the Osa Group (late Pliocene) and Puerto Jiménez Group (late Pleistocene–Holocene) gravels. Useful for sediment provenance as well as for the mining history of the Osa.
verbatim_finding: The Golfo Dulce goldfield has been mined since pre-Colombian times and during the 1980's produced at least twice as much gold as the entire Tilarán-Aguacate Gold Province in northern Costa Rica.
data_availability: Heavy-mineral suites, gold habit/composition data and geographic-stratigraphic distribution maps are given in the paper. Scanned PDF free from UCR; no digital dataset.
caveat: The 'Nicoya Complex' label used here for the Osa basement has since been superseded; Buchs et al. (2009) show these rocks are exotic accreted seamounts and plateau fragments (Osa Igneous Complex), unrelated to the Nicoya Complex proper. Scanned PDF, no text layer.

title: Occurrence and distribution patterns of several marine vertebrates in Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The broadest single-effort baseline for marine megafauna in the gulf: 55 daily sighting surveys across two seasons (January–February 2010, July–August 2011), 423.7 observation hours, 458 sightings and at least 30 marine species, combined with 82 interviews of fishers and tour guides. Rather than treating any one taxon in depth, it maps where whales, dolphins, sea turtles and sea snakes concentrate, identifying high-density areas within the embayment by GIS analysis and confirming that animals use the inlet for foraging, mating, resting and socialising rather than merely passing through. It is the natural entry point for anyone asking 'what is actually in Golfo Dulce, and where'.
verbatim_finding: A total of 458 recorded sightings, representing at least 30 marine species, were acquired during 423.7 observation hours across all areas of the embayment.
data_availability: Sighting counts by species and GIS-derived density maps published in the open-access article; interview transcripts not deposited.
caveat: Two short seasonal windows a year and a half apart; interview-derived records are not independently verified.

title: A new subspecies of sea snake, Hydrophis platurus xanthos, from Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The clearest case in the literature of Golfo Dulce's physical structure producing an endemic form. From 154 specimens gathered 2010–2017, the authors describe a yellow, small-bodied subspecies of the pelagic sea snake restricted to roughly 320 km² of the gulf's inner basin — waters the paper itself characterises as occasionally anoxic. They argue that bathymetry (the shallow sill) restricts gene flow to conspecifics in the wider eastern Pacific, and document behaviour unlike any reported for the species: no association with drift lines, and nocturnal sinusoidal ambush feeding in turbulent water. The taxon is proposed as an evolutionarily significant unit warranting protection.
verbatim_finding: We describe a distinctive new subspecies of sea snake from the occasionally anoxic inner-basin waters of Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
data_availability: Morphometric and colour-pattern data for 154 specimens (123 free-ranging, 31 museum-held) with supplementary material deposited alongside the open-access article; type material lodged in museum collections.
caveat: Subspecies status is diagnosed on morphology, colour and bathymetric isolation rather than on molecular data; the taxonomic rank has been discussed critically since publication, and the same first author later revisited the population's natural history (see Solórzano-López & Sasa 2024, Rev. Biol. Trop.).

title: The value and limitations of local ecological knowledge: Longitudinal and retrospective assessment of flagship species in Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The one rigorous test located of what Golfo Dulce fishers and boat guides actually know about their own water, and how far it can be trusted. Interviews conducted in 2010 and repeated in 2020 with fishermen and tour guides were compared directly against boat-based sighting surveys run in the same two periods, for cetaceans, sea turtles, whale sharks and sea snakes. The design — the same questions, the same observers' community, a decade apart, with an independent biological baseline — is what makes it usable both as a record of local knowledge and as a calibration of it.
verbatim_finding: Local ecological knowledge (LEK), obtained from experienced residents, can complement other approaches and provide improved understanding of the conservation status of marine areas.
data_availability: Open access under the British Ecological Society. Two rounds of structured interviews (2010, 2020) plus paired boat-based sighting-survey data for Golfo Dulce; see the article's data-availability statement for the deposited records.
caveat: The Wiley landing page blocks automated access (HTTP 403); metadata and the quoted abstract came from the Crossref record. The study covers only charismatic species of tourism interest, so it is not a general test of fisher knowledge about fish stocks or place names.

title: La Ley Indígena de 1977 en Costa Rica: origen y negociación en el contexto de los años 1970
summary: Explains the legal instrument that still governs the relationship between the Costa Rican state and the Boruca, Térraba, Ngäbe and other peoples of the southern Pacific — the 1977 Ley Indígena and the reserve system it entrenched. Working from legislative files, decrees, press of the 1960s–70s and an interview with one of the law's promoters, Boza shows the law was not a sudden reform but the outcome of a debate reaching back to the late 1930s and, in some respects, to the colonial period, driven by media attention to indigenous dispossession and by unusual cross-party support in the Assembly.
verbatim_finding: Se argumenta que la aprobación de la Ley Indígena no fue un evento aislado, sino parte de una discusión legal y política sobre los derechos indígenas cuyos orígenes se remontan a finales de la década de 1930
data_availability: Open access. Documentary base is described in detail (laws and executive decrees, the legislative expediente for the bill, related normative files, one oral-history interview, Costa Rican press 1960s–70s); the archival material itself is held in Costa Rican state archives.
caveat: National legal history — it does not treat any single southern-zone territory in depth, and the article notes that indigenous people had little direct hand in drafting the text.

title: Riparian vegetation reduces coastal turbidity
summary: Uses 33 years of remote sensing (1987–2019) over southern Costa Rica, including Golfo Dulce, with four causal-inference methods to quantify how catchment land use propagates into the gulf's water column as turbidity. It finds that a 15 m riparian natural-vegetation buffer significantly reduces gulf turbidity out to 800 m offshore, while pasture and gravel roads increase it, and that effects are strongest for short, steep or low-discharge rivers. Watershed-scale land-use composition, by contrast, showed no significant effect. This is the only source giving a multi-decadal, spatially explicit account of the terrestrial control on Golfo Dulce's surface optical properties.
verbatim_finding: We found that riparian natural vegetation (15 m buffer) significantly reduced gulf turbidity up to 800 m offshore, which overlaps with coral reefs and seagrass habitats.
data_availability: Open access (Nature Portfolio). Built on public Landsat archives and land-cover products; the paper's data and code availability statements point to the derived turbidity and land-use datasets.
caveat: Satellite-derived turbidity is a surface optical proxy, not a measured suspended-sediment load, and says nothing about the deeper water column or the anoxic layer.

title: Late Cretaceous to Miocene seamount accretion and mélange formation in the Osa and Burica Peninsulas (Southern Costa Rica): episodic growth of a convergent margin
summary: The modern definition of the basement terranes flanking Golfo Dulce, and the paper that replaced the old 'Nicoya Complex' label on Osa. It separates the Osa Igneous Complex — an accretionary prism sensu stricto of basaltic lavas, sills, gabbros, pelagic limestones and radiolarites, containing no upper-plate-derived material — from the overlying Osa Mélange. Four units, in contact along reactivated palaeo-décollements, comprise Coniacian–Santonian oceanic plateau fragments (Inner Osa Igneous Complex) and Coniacian–Santonian to Middle Eocene seamounts (Outer Osa Igneous Complex). These are shown to be exotic with respect to the Caribbean Plate and unrelated to other Costa Rican and Panamanian igneous complexes, having been accreted in discrete episodes alternating with periods of tectonic erosion. The mélange is dominated by Late Eocene debris flows and hemipelagites, i.e. large-scale submarine mass wasting of the margin.
verbatim_finding: Multidisciplinary study of the Osa and Burica peninsulas, Costa Rica, recognizes the Osa Igneous Complex and the Osa Mélange – records of a complex Late Cretaceous–Miocene tectonic–sedimentary history.
data_availability: Geochemical analyses (including LA-ICP-MS), radiolarian and foraminiferal biostratigraphy and geological maps are in the chapter and its supplements. An author-deposited green open-access copy is available via SERVAL (University of Lausanne).
caveat: Written partly as a rebuttal of Vannucchi et al. (2006); the extent of true mélange versus coherent accreted crust on Osa remains contested.

title: Ethnoecological Importance Value (EIV) Methodology: Assessing the cultural importance of ecosystems as sources of useful plants for the Guaymi people of Costa Rica
summary: The most substantive quantitative record found of Ngäbe (Guaymí) environmental knowledge in the Costa Rican south Pacific. Fieldwork in the Guaymí Indigenous Reserve of Coto Brus, on the inland flank of the Golfo Dulce watershed, combined free-listing interviews with 46 community members and vegetation sampling across five successional stages, yielding 53 recorded wild food plant species and one fungus, with the cognitive domain estimated at 63 species. It introduces the EIV index, which weights each species' cultural salience by its measured abundance — a transferable method for valuing habitats by the knowledge attached to them.
verbatim_finding: To the Guaymi, the most culturally valuable successional stages, in terms of being sources of wild edible plants, were the mature forests and their edges.
data_availability: Open-access PDF, pp. 249–257, with the species list, free-list salience values and successional-stage abundance results reported in the article. Raw interview data are not deposited.
caveat: Terrestrial and plant-focused: it records forest knowledge, not marine or fisher knowledge, and the Coto Brus reserve is upslope from the gulf rather than on it. Sample of 46 informants in one reserve.

title: Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica, un área importante de alimentación para la tortuga carey del Pacífico Oriental (Eretmochelys imbricata)
summary: In-water capture study (August 2010 – March 2013) establishing Golfo Dulce as a foraging ground for the critically endangered eastern Pacific hawksbill: 62 captures including 14 recaptures, three-quarters of them juveniles, all untagged elsewhere. Two findings matter beyond the head-count. First, detection probability was much higher in the dry season, which the authors attribute to seasonal turbidity from river sediment loads — a direct link between the gulf's terrestrial runoff regime and turtle habitat quality. Second, 45 % of animals carried the ectoparasitic barnacle Stephanolepas muricata. The authors describe this as the longest and most robust in-water hawksbill monitoring dataset in the eastern tropical Pacific.
verbatim_finding: Our findings highlight the relevance of the Golfo Dulce as an important foraging ground for hawksbill turtles in the ETP
data_availability: Capture-per-unit-effort by season, carapace-length distributions and recapture records are tabulated in the open-access article; individual tag records held by the field programme.
caveat: Entanglement-net capture along mangrove and seagrass edges only, so the sample is biased toward those habitats; seasonal detection differences may reflect water clarity rather than genuine turtle absence.

title: Captura por unidad de esfuerzo y estructura poblacional de la tortuga verde de Pacífico (Chelonia mydas) en el Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: Companion study to the hawksbill work, capturing 253 green turtles (20 recaptures) in the western sector of the gulf between 2010 and 2013. Its distinctive contributions are the international connectivity — one recaptured female had been tagged in the Galápagos, and the authors infer adult females originating from nesting beaches in Panama and Colombia — and the record of a mass mortality event in January 2013 that appears in the declining CPUE series. The paper explicitly frames Golfo Dulce's mangrove, reef and seagrass mosaic as the feeding resource holding these animals, and proposes turtles as an umbrella species for gulf-wide protection.
verbatim_finding: Our results suggest that the Golfo Dulce is an important area for green turtles, where individuals congregate for adults and subadults would feed on seagrasses and the fleshy parts of the mangroves.
data_availability: Annual CPUE series (0.19–0.45), curved carapace length distributions and tag/recapture records reported in the open-access article.
caveat: CPUE decline is confounded with the January 2013 mortality event and with net-based sampling at a single western site; the Galápagos link rests on one recaptured individual.

title: CONSTRUCCIÓN SOCIAL DEL PAISAJE DEL TERRITORIO INDÍGENA TÉRRABA, BUENOS AIRES, COSTA RICA
summary: A life-history study of how the Térraba (Brörán) people themselves narrate the transformation of their territory between 1940 and 2015, based on three collective accounts gathered in Térraba centro, Murciélago and Las Parcelas plus individual testimony from key informants. It is the best-documented account located of indigenous landscape knowledge in the Río Grande de Térraba basin — the river system whose delta holds the World Heritage sphere sites and whose sediment discharge reaches the coast beside Golfo Dulce — and it ties landscape change explicitly to labour, everyday life and land struggle rather than to abstract land-cover change.
verbatim_finding: Los resultados muestran la manera en que se ha modificado el paisaje de este territorio, producto del trabajo, la vida cotidiana y las luchas sociales en el período de 1940-2015.
data_availability: Open-access PDF, ePUB and HTML. Qualitative: three collective life-story accounts and individual interviews, summarised in the article; transcripts are not deposited.
caveat: Térraba territory is inland in the Buenos Aires canton, on the river rather than on Golfo Dulce itself; use it for indigenous relations to the watershed, not to the gulf shoreline.

title: EL DESARROLLO DEL BANANO Y LA PALMA ACEITERA EN EL PACÍFICO COSTARRICENSE DESDE LA PERSPECTIVA DE LA ECOLOGÍA HISTÓRICA
summary: The key source for the crop succession that defines the modern landscape around Golfo Dulce: bananas out, African oil palm in. Clare reads both crops through historical ecology, treating the plantation not as an economic unit but as an ecological regime with its own soil, disease and labour consequences, and follows the transition on the Costa Rican Pacific from the United Fruit period into the palma africana era that replaced it after the 1984–85 withdrawal. It supplies the environmental-history framing that the purely economic literature on the enclave lacks.
verbatim_finding: El artículo pretende abordar desde la perspectiva de la Ecología Histórica, el desarrollo de los cultivos del banano y la palma en el en el Pacífico Costarricense
data_availability: Open-access PDF and HTML in Diálogos vol. 6 no. 1 (2005). Synthetic historical study; no primary dataset. Keywords: Ecología, banano, palma africana, historia, economía, sociedad.
caveat: Twenty years old; the oil-palm expansion it describes has continued and intensified since, so the quantitative picture is dated even where the framing holds. The published abstract contains a typographical duplication ('en el en el').

title: EL CASO DEL PUEBLO CIVIL DE GOLFITO, UNA RESPUESTA ESTATAL A LA MERCANTILIZACIÓN DEL BANANO EN EL PACÍFICO SUR COSTARRICENSE (1938-1964)
summary: The most recent and most archivally grounded study of how Golfito actually grew. It separates the company town proper from the 'Pueblo Civil' — the unplanned settlement of Costa Ricans outside United Fruit's fenced zone — and shows the state, not the company, having to create, build and service it, with the INVU taking over from 1954. Sources are the Costa Rican national archive, the 1930s banana contracts, business records of the Golfito division, INVU annual reports and local and regional press, which makes it the best documentary entry point to the port's rise between 1938 and the mid-1960s.
verbatim_finding: El objetivo del artículo es analizar el origen y desarrollo del espacio denominado como Pueblo Civil en el cantón de Golfito durante el periodo 1938-1962.
data_availability: Open access. Primary sources named explicitly (Archivo Nacional de Costa Rica, 1930s banana contracts, Golfito division company documents, INVU memorias, regional press); no digital dataset, but the archival trail is fully specified.
caveat: Title and abstract disagree on the end date (1964 vs 1962). Covers the growth phase only — it stops well before the 1985 withdrawal and the port's abandonment.

title: Península de Osa — Ocupaciones precolombinas de la Península de Osa
container: Museo Nacional de Costa Rica, Departamento de Antropología e Historia
summary: The single most directly relevant synthesis of pre-Columbian settlement on the land that encloses Golfo Dulce, from the national archaeological authority. It reports that Osa has been very lightly surveyed despite its auriferous rivers, sets out two occupation periods — Aguas Buenas (300 BC–AD 800) and Chiriquí (AD 800–1500) — and describes the mound site Cantarero (P-35-Ct) on the Río Tigre as the best-studied settlement, with subordinate satellite sites (Cantarito 1–4) suggesting a territorial hierarchy. It links the modern orero gold-panning economy directly to the archaeological record: it was looting damage at Cantarero in 2015 that triggered the current survey programme.
verbatim_finding: la península destaca, además de su biodiversidad, por la presencia de ríos con arenas auríferas que fueron ampliamente aprovechados por las sociedades precolombinas
data_availability: Narrative report with site maps drawn from the MNCR 'Orígenes' national site database, site photographs, and a downloadable bibliography; the underlying site records are held by the museum and are request-required.
caveat: Institutional web report rather than peer-reviewed publication; the page itself states that no systematic regional survey of the peninsula has yet been done, so distributions are provisional.

title: Forearc response to subduction of the Cocos Ridge, Panama-Costa Rica
summary: The foundational subsidence-then-uplift history for the two peninsulas that enclose Golfo Dulce, and the source of the basin's Pliocene deep-water phase. Depth-diagnostic foraminifera in a ~3 000 m thick Pliocene–Pleistocene turbidite sequence on Burica document rapid Pliocene subsidence on a south-dipping palaeoslope, then shoaling from 2 000+ m to 1 200 m during the late Pliocene, with present exposure implying ~1 mm/yr average Quaternary uplift. The section is correlated to equivalent marine strata on Osa. The paper also names the Ballena-Celmira fault zone, the margin-parallel structure bounding the arcward side of Osa and Burica that has taken up vertical displacement between the outer forearc and the Térraba inner forearc through the Tertiary, and attributes Neogene deformation to isostatic uplift from Cocos Ridge subduction beginning about 1 Ma.
verbatim_finding: document rapid Pliocene subsidence and basin infilling followed by Quaternary deformation and uplift
data_availability: Foraminiferal palaeobathymetry, measured stratigraphic sections and structural data are presented in the paper. No deposited dataset; GSA paywall (PDF only).
caveat: The 1 Ma onset date for Cocos Ridge subduction is now regarded as too young; later work (Silver et al. 2004; Zeumann & Hampel 2017; Vannucchi et al. 2006) argues for onset between ~8 Ma and ~1.8 Ma.

title: Los arrecifes coralinos de Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica: aspectos geológicos
summary: The only Holocene sediment record actually recovered and dated from inside Golfo Dulce, and therefore the closest thing the gulf has to a palaeoenvironmental archive. Nine core holes and four sediment cores through the Punta Islotes fringing reef show at least 9 m of reef, growing on an uneven Cretaceous basalt surface, with radiocarbon dates placing initiation at about 5 500 yr B.P. — i.e. after post-glacial sea level had approached its present position. Accumulation rates are quantified by facies (reef-flat branching coral 1.6–2.4 m/1000 yr; fore-reef massive coral 0.9–8.3 m/1000 yr; fore-reef talus 0.07–0.3 m/1000 yr) and growth is divided into four stages, the last showing collapse in accumulation attributed first to freshwater input and more recently to terrigenous sediment from deforestation.
verbatim_finding: se reconstruyó con información obtenida de nueve perforaciones y cuatro núcleos de sedimentos colectados a lo largo de cuatro transectos en el frente del arrecife
data_availability: Radiocarbon dates, core logs and facies-specific accumulation rates are tabulated in the paper. Scanned PDF freely available from the UCR archive; no deposited dataset.
caveat: Bilingual (Spanish resumen and English abstract). Covers only the reef framework at Punta Islotes, not the deep anoxic basin. Scanned PDF, no text layer.

title: Informe Nacional para las Comisiones Hidrográficas Regionales — Costa Rica 2024 (MACHC25)
container: 25ª Conferencia de la Comisión Hidrográfica Mesoamericana y del Mar Caribe (MACHC25), Organización Hidrográfica Internacional
summary: Costa Rica's own account, in Spanish, of its hydrographic capacity — and the reason no modern survey of Golfo Dulce exists. The state has no dedicated hydrographic office: soundings are done piecemeal by the MOPT's Proceso de Hidrografía y Topografía for port works and siltation control, and by IMARES-UCR. The report states plainly that there are no vessels for large-scale bathymetry, no specialised equipment for it, no capacity for satellite-derived or crowdsourced bathymetry, no recent updates to national paper charts, and no update to submit to IHO C-55. A National Hydrographic Committee was still being formed in 2024. This is the institutional explanation for the 90%-unsurveyed figure.
verbatim_finding: No se cuenta con buques específicos para llevar a cabo batimetrías a gran escala.
data_availability: Lists topo-bathymetric surveys carried out by PHT-DOMP-MOPT from 2021 onward (an activity recorded since 1973); all are port-works and siltation surveys, none in Golfo Dulce. No data are published or distributed. Free PDF on the IHO server.
caveat: The report carries no named author; it is a state submission to a regional IHO commission. Its survey list covers 2021 onward only, so it cannot by itself rule out an older national survey of the gulf.

title: Distribución y condiciones ambientales asociadas al comportamiento del delfín bufeo (Tursiops truncatus) y el delfín manchado (Stenella attenuata) (Cetacea: Delphinidae) en el Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: A behaviour-by-habitat study (June 1996 – July 1997) that ties dolphin activity to specific coastal features rather than to open-water conditions. Bottlenose dolphin foraging coincided exclusively with river mouths, coral reefs and mangrove edges, and the animals rarely crossed the gulf (16.56 % of travelling bouts), implying side-fidelity within the embayment. For spotted dolphins no such association emerged. The paper's own explanation for the weak statistical signal is itself informative about the system: the author attributes it in part to the environmental homogeneity of Golfo Dulce's surface layer, which is what one expects in a strongly stratified basin where the interesting gradients are vertical rather than horizontal.
verbatim_finding: For the bottlenose dolphin, foraging/feeding activities showed exclusive coincidence with river mouths, coral reef and mangrove areas, while social and milling activities where seen close to feeding areas.
data_availability: Behavioural sampling records, group-size statistics and ANOVA results are reported in the open-access PDF; no raw data deposit.
caveat: One year of observation; the negative results (no significant activity–environment associations) rest on modest sample sizes (n=156 bottlenose, n=51 spotted behavioural bouts). A parallel English-language version appeared in Investigaciones Marinas 35(2).

title: N2 production by the anammox reaction in the anoxic water column of Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The paper that made Golfo Dulce globally significant. Using 15N labelling in the anoxic water column, it showed that anaerobic ammonium oxidation — previously known mainly from sediments and engineered reactors — accounts for 19–35% of N2 production in a marine water column. Because Golfo Dulce's chemistry closely resembles that of open-ocean oxygen minimum zones, where a third to a half of global fixed-nitrogen removal occurs, this small Costa Rican basin became the proof of concept that anammox is a major term in the ocean nitrogen budget. Every subsequent OMZ nitrogen study cites it.
verbatim_finding: Here we show that this reaction is also important in the anoxic waters of Golfo Dulce, a 200-m-deep coastal bay in Costa Rica, where it accounts for 19-35% of the total N2 formation in the water column.
data_availability: Rate measurements and depth profiles presented in the figures; supplementary information on the Nature site. No raw data deposit.
caveat: Based on incubations from a limited number of casts. The 19–35% share is specific to Golfo Dulce at that time; anammox-vs-denitrification partitioning is known to vary strongly between and within OMZs.

title: Esferas precolombinas de la zona sur en Costa Rica: cultura y poder en la tecnología de la piedra
summary: A critical-historiographical reading of the Diquís spheres that is unusually useful for a public hub because it treats the spheres as objects with a modern political life, not only an ancient one. It traces how the spheres were mobilised as media spectacle, as props of Costa Rican national identity, and — the point that connects directly to the Golfito story — as rallying objects for a banana-plantation community, since it was United Fruit's clearing of the Diquís delta in the 1930s–40s that exposed most of them. It also reviews the institutional mishandling of the archaeological patrimony.
verbatim_finding: En la primera parte se describen algunas de las dinámicas simbólicas del poder en las que estos enigmáticos objetos se han visto involucrados
data_availability: Open-access PDF, pp. 70–83. Interpretive essay: no primary datasets, measurements or site inventories; it works from previously published sphere archaeology.
caveat: Aesthetic and cultural-studies analysis rather than archaeology; use it for the reception history of the spheres, not for their chronology or manufacture.

title: Carta Esferica desde el Golfo Dulce en la Costa Rica hasa Sn. Blas en la Nueva Galicia
summary: The deepest layer of the charting record for this coast, and it starts at Golfo Dulce: the Spanish Hydrographic Office's 1822 sheet takes the gulf as its southern limit and runs north to San Blas at 1:2,800,000, built on the 1789-1794 Malaspina expedition. It establishes that the gulf entered European hydrography as an endpoint on a passage chart rather than as a place to be surveyed, and that the first systematic soundings of this coast were made under sail more than two centuries ago. At that scale the whole gulf is a few millimetres wide; it fixes the coastline, not the sea floor.
verbatim_finding: Representing the most advanced data available to the Spanish Admiralty at the time, this 1822 Direccion Hidrografía nautical chart or maritime map details the Pacific coast of Central America from southern Mexico and Guatemala to Costa Rica.
data_availability: Original sheet held privately (this copy sold); a high-resolution TIFF scan is offered for purchase by the dealer. No soundings in digital form.
caveat: Retrieved from an antiquarian map dealer, so the descriptive text quoted is the dealer's, not the chart's. Title and 1:2,800,000 scale are read off the sheet itself in the listing. The chart is included as evidence of charting lineage, not as a source of depths.

title: Pleistocene vertical motions of the Costa Rican outer forearc from subducting topography and a migrating fracture zone triple junction
summary: Uses 3D seismic sequence stratigraphy from the CRISP reflection volume offshore southern Costa Rica to date and separate the processes that raise and drop the outer forearc adjacent to Golfo Dulce. Three major shelf and slope erosional events are resolved at ca. 2.5–2.3, 1.95–1.78 and 1.78–1.19 Ma, each producing abrupt shifts in sedimentation pattern and rate. Three mechanisms are distinguished: regional subaerial erosion and rapid subsidence tied to southeastward migration of the Panama Fracture Zone triple junction; transient kilometre-scale uplift and subsidence from subducting plate topography; and progressive outer-wedge shortening on landward- and seaward-dipping thrusts driven by the impinging Cocos Ridge. The finding that parts of the shelf were subaerially eroded is directly relevant to reconstructing former, now-submerged coastlines.
verbatim_finding: regional subaerial erosion and rapid subsidence linked to the southeastward Panama Fracture Zone triple-junction migration, with associated abrupt bathymetric variations and plate kinematic changes
data_availability: Interpretation of the CRISP 3D seismic-reflection volume; horizon maps, isochrons and volume calculations in the paper. Gold open access — free PDF at pubs.geoscienceworld.org/geosphere/article-pdf/14/2/510/4101799/510.pdf. Underlying CRISP seismic data are archived by the Academic Seismic Portal (UTIG).
caveat: The CRISP volume lies on the outer shelf and slope offshore Osa, not inside Golfo Dulce itself; the erosional events are Pleistocene and much older than the gulf's present configuration.

title: "Marine Areas of Responsible Fishing": A Path Toward Small-Scale Fisheries Co-Management in Costa Rica? Perspectives from Golfo Dulce
summary: The only substantial scholarly assessment of the AMPR instrument itself as a governance experiment, using Golfo Dulce as the principal case. It reads the Costa Rican Marine Areas of Responsible Fishing against the co-management literature in a state where fisheries governance has been centralised, top-down and data-poor, and asks whether the AMPR genuinely devolves authority to fisher organisations or reproduces the same asymmetry under a participatory label. This is the reference to cite when characterising the AMPR Golfo Dulce as something other than a protected area, and Molina-Ureña (CIMAR/UCR) is a direct institutional link into the gulf.
verbatim_finding: This chapter analyzes participatory management processes of small-scale fisheries in two Pacific embayments of Costa Rica, a centralized state of Central America where fisheries management is traditionally "top-down", data deficient, and poorly adapted
data_availability: None distributed. Analysis rests on interviews and documentary review reported in the chapter text, which is behind the Springer paywall.
caveat: Paywalled — only the publisher's truncated abstract could be read, so the quoted sentence is the abstract as displayed and is cut off by Springer, not by us. Full assessment of the chapter's findings requires the book.

title: Biogeochemical controls on the oxygen, nitrogen and sulfur distributions in the water column of Golfo Dulce: an anoxic basin on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica revisited
summary: The full synthesis of the 1994 water-column and sediment biogeochemistry, and the paper that puts numbers on the renewal question. It reports the deepest ~100 m as anoxic with sulfide below 7 µM and only transiently present, bacterial maxima where oxygen falls below 1 µM around 100 m, and a sub-pycnocline dissolved inorganic nitrogen deficit of 2.9 mol m-2. Combined with a salt-balance residence time of 35 ± 57 days it yields a DIN loss of 51 ± 85 mmol m-2 d-1. It also explains the two reasons sulfide never builds up: frequent oxygenated Pacific inflows in the water column, and scavenging by iron-rich turbidites in the sediment, the most recent emplaced between 1989 and 1992 on 210Pb dating.
verbatim_finding: Sulfide in the water column was maintained at low concentrations by frequent inputs of oxygenated water from the Pacific Ocean.
data_availability: Chemical profiles, respiration rates, bacterial counts and 210Pb sediment chronology are tabulated and plotted in the article. No separate data deposit; a copy is also held in the University of Southern Denmark research portal.
caveat: The residence-time estimate (35 ± 57 d) has an uncertainty larger than the estimate itself, so the derived DIN-loss rate should be treated as order-of-magnitude. Journal DOI does not resolve.

title: Localización del naufragio del SV Viduco durante la prospección arqueológica subacuática en Isla del Coco. Campaña de elaboración de la carta arqueológica subacuática de Costa Rica
summary: The methodological template for what a Golfo Dulce underwater survey would look like, and the clearest statement of how recent this work is in Costa Rica. It reports the first underwater archaeological prospection carried out at Isla del Coco — 2,400 ha of land against 97,235 ha of marine area — within the national programme to build a Carta Arqueológica Subacuática de Costa Rica, and the location and study of a wreck tentatively identified as the SV Viduco. The authors state plainly that cultural, as opposed to biological, research on Costa Rican waters is recent, which is why no comparable survey exists for the southern Pacific gulfs.
verbatim_finding: tratamos de dar a conocer los resultados obtenidos en la primera prospección arqueológica subacuática realizada en la Isla del Coco y la localización y estudio de uno de sus pecios, el tentativamente identificado como el SV Viduco
data_availability: Open PDF (2.0 MB) downloadable from figshare, item 12236591. Volume I of the Carta Arqueológica Subacuática de Costa Rica (Lozano Guerra-Librero & Fernández López) covers the same Isla del Coco prospection in full. Figshare assigns a DataCite DOI (10.6084/m9.figshare.12236591.v1) which is not registered with Crossref, so it is not recorded in the doi field here.
caveat: Isla del Coco, ~550 km offshore, not Golfo Dulce — included as the only located example of Costa Rican Pacific underwater archaeology and as evidence of the national survey programme. Self-deposited preprint, not peer reviewed; the Viduco identification is explicitly tentative.

title: Preliminary analysis of the fish species of the Pacific Central American Mangrove of Zancudo, Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The only dedicated fish-community survey of a Golfo Dulce mangrove. Eighty-two species in 30 families were recorded at Zancudo, of which more than half are estuarine transients and only 14 are estuarine residents — evidence that the mangrove functions primarily as a transition and nursery corridor rather than as a self-contained assemblage. Crucially for fisheries policy, 71 % of the species captured are of first- or second-grade commercial value and only 11 % have none, so mangrove loss translates almost directly into lost catch. Multidimensional scaling shows the community reorganising from river mouth to inner channels and between rainy and dry seasons, driven by salinity gradients.
verbatim_finding: Eighty-two species belonging to 30 families were identified. More than half of them belonged to the estuarine transient fish group and only 14 species were estuarine resident
data_availability: Species list with seasonal abundances and MDS ordinations are in the article; not deposited openly.
caveat: Explicitly preliminary; one mangrove system, limited seasonal replication, and the authors call for further work on temporal variation.

title: Evaluación preliminar del área agrícola y su influencia sobre la calidad del agua en el Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The quantitative backbone for the agricultural-runoff argument, and the only study that puts numbers on the pesticide load reaching the gulf. Working across the Esquinas, Coto Colorado, Rincón, Conte, Agujas, Tigre and Palma sub-basins, the authors map roughly 10 000 ha of rice and 31 000 ha of African oil palm from satellite imagery, estimate annual pesticide application at 20.4 kg/ha for rice and 6.6 kg/ha for oil palm plus 840 kg/ha/yr of granular fertiliser, and then confirm residues analytically in water, sediment and fish. Clomazone was detected in every water sample; triazophos, isoprothiolane and propiconazole appeared in the Coto Colorado sub-basin, which alone carries 95% of the agricultural area draining to the gulf. From IRET, Universidad Nacional.
verbatim_finding: Se determinó el área de los cultivos, mediante interpretación de imágenes satelitales, para un total aproximado de 10 000 ha de arroz Oryza sativa y 31 000 ha de palma aceitera Elaeis guineensis.
data_availability: Crop areas by sub-basin, estimated application rates and GC-MS / LC-DAD residue detections are tabulated in the open-access article. Raw chromatographic data are not deposited.
caveat: Explicitly preliminary: residue sampling was a single point-in-time campaign, and application rates are estimated from secondary sources and producer surveys rather than measured. Crossref records the issue as 2018 while the journal landing page dates it 2019-01-01.

title: Determination of Respiration Rates in Water with Sub-Micromolar Oxygen Concentrations
summary: A methods paper that matters for interpreting every oxygen-consumption number reported from Golfo Dulce. Using water from the Golfo Dulce anoxic basin alongside Chile–Peru OMZ water and nanomolar-sensitivity optode measurements, it shows that laboratory incubation artefacts inflate measured O2 consumption rates by 3 to 60 times as incubations are prolonged, with the inflation starting after 4–5 h in surface water and 10–15 h below the mixed layer, and that deoxygenation by gas bubbling and stirring further distort rates. It is the reason older long-incubation respiration estimates for low-oxygen waters should be treated as upper bounds.
verbatim_finding: we have explored how experimental conditions affect measured rates of O2 consumption in low-O2 waters from the anoxic basin of Golfo Dulce (Costa Rica) and oceanic waters off Chile-Peru
data_availability: Incubation time series and derived rates presented in figures. Open access under Frontiers CC-BY; no separate data repository deposit.
caveat: Methodological rather than descriptive — it uses Golfo Dulce water as material, and reports no new hydrography for the gulf.

title: Quaternary uplift astride the aseismic Cocos Ridge, Pacific coast, Costa Rica
summary: Quantifies the uplift that is raising the walls of Golfo Dulce and provides the regional context in which the gulf's drowned relief must be read. Radiocarbon-dated Holocene marine terraces and beach-ridge complexes, together with the Plio-Pleistocene stratigraphic record, show maximum crustal uplift on the Península de Osa — immediately landward of where the aseismic Cocos Ridge enters the trench — decreasing northwest toward Nicoya and southeast toward Burica. Rates on Osa decrease systematically from 6.5 to 2.1 m/ka across the peninsula, which the authors model as uplifted fault blocks tilting down to the northeast at 0.03–0.06° per thousand years. An elastic-plate model reproduces the pattern with a truncated Cocos Ridge subducted ~50 km over the last 0.5 m.y. beneath a plate of 5 km effective elastic thickness. The northeastward tilt of Osa toward the gulf is directly relevant to why Golfo Dulce is deepest on its inner side.
verbatim_finding: The Pliocene and Pleistocene stratigraphic record and Holocene marine terraces and beach ridge complexes indicate that maximum rates of crustal uplift have occurred on the Península de Osa, immediately landward of the aseismic Cocos Ridge.
data_availability: Radiocarbon date compilations, terrace elevations and uplift-rate calculations are tabulated in the paper; flexural model parameters given. No deposited dataset; GSA paywall (PDF only).
caveat: The shape of the subducted end of the Cocos Ridge is unknown, so the flexural model tests two scenarios; the preferred truncated-ridge model is non-unique. Uplift rates on Nicoya are described by the authors as less well constrained.

title: Upper-plate deformation in response to flat slab subduction inboard of the aseismic Cocos Ridge, Osa Peninsula, Costa Rica
summary: The most detailed modern account of how the Osa Peninsula deforms, and the best explanation available for why the local topography and the shape of Golfo Dulce vary so sharply over short distances. Combining eight new radiocarbon ages, five OSL ages and ten previously published radiocarbon ages, it shows late Quaternary uplift rates of 1.7–8.5 m/k.y., and demonstrates that modern topography, basement (Osa Mélange) elevation, elevation of Quaternary marine deposits (Marenco formation) and uplift-rate distribution all directly mirror the bathymetry of the subducting Cocos Ridge, whose relief locally exceeds 1 km. Deformation is modelled as a thin outer-margin wedge responding by simple shear on subvertical faults to short-wavelength, high-relief asperities on the downgoing plate, rather than by margin-perpendicular shortening.
verbatim_finding: The Osa Peninsula is fragmented into small (~5 km), independently deforming blocks bounded by trench-parallel and trench-perpendicular, subvertical, normal and reverse faults that extend down to the plate interface, allowing for greatly different deformation histories over short distances.
data_availability: Radiocarbon and OSL ages, terrace and marine-deposit elevations, and uplift-rate calculations are tabulated. Free (bronze OA) PDF at pubs.geoscienceworld.org/gsa/lithosphere/article-pdf/5/3/247/3050422/247.pdf.

title: Investigating Pre-Columbian Gold and Copper in Costa Rica – Ores, Mines and Artefact Production
summary: Fills the largest gap in the region's metallurgical story: where the gold in the famous Chiriquí-period goldwork actually came from. The team combines mining-archaeological prospection with geochemical provenance analysis of ores and artefacts, and identifies four major gold and copper districts with distinct mineralisation types as fieldwork targets. For Golfo Dulce this is the scientific bridge between the placer geology of the Osa peninsula and the pre-Columbian objects held in Costa Rican museums, and it makes explicit how little was previously known about pre-conquest mining in the country.
verbatim_finding: The name of Costa Rica itself, in fact alludes to the large numbers of golden metal objects worn by the indigenous peoples upon arrival of the conquistadors.
data_availability: Open-access PDF with maps of the four ore districts and description of the analytical protocol (geochemical fingerprinting of ores and artefacts). Full analytical datasets are not deposited with the article; the project is ongoing.
caveat: Interim project report — provenance assignments are presented as work in progress, and the Osa/Golfo Dulce placer district is one of four, not the sole focus.

title: GEBCO_2026 Grid: General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans gridded bathymetry data
authors: General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans
container: General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans / British Oceanographic Data Centre
summary: The global grid that everything else in this gulf ultimately rests on, including GMRT's fill layer. Its cell size is 15 arc-seconds — roughly 460 m of longitude at 8.5°N — so a single GEBCO cell spans about a fifth of the width of the Golfo Dulce sill. GEBCO ships a companion Type Identifier (TID) grid precisely because most cells are not measured: the TID codes distinguish direct soundings from predicted, interpolated and pre-generated values. Anyone quoting a Golfo Dulce depth from GEBCO is quoting an interpolation unless the TID for that cell says otherwise, and the coverage analysis for this gulf indicates it very rarely does.
verbatim_finding: a global terrain model for ocean and land, providing elevation data, in meters, on a 15 arc-second interval grid
data_availability: Free download as netCDF, GeoTIFF, Esri ASCII and data GeoTIFF, globally or by user-defined area, plus the separate TID grid identifying each cell's source type. Current release GEBCO_2026, published 23 April 2026, DOI 10.5285/4f68d5c7-45eb-f999-e063-7086abc036fa (DataCite, resolvable at doi.org).
caveat: The DataCite DOI is recorded in the text rather than the doi field because it is not a Crossref record. 15 arc-seconds is a grid spacing, not a resolution claim: in a gulf this size the grid is finer than the data behind it.

title: Global Multi-Resolution Topography (GMRT) Synthesis, version 4.5.0
authors: Marine Geoscience Data System, Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory
summary: The best-available open bathymetric compilation for the gulf, and the one whose own documentation explains why it is thin here. GMRT curates cleaned ship multibeam at ~120 m and blends it over a base of GEBCO 2026 at 15 arc-seconds; a mask layer marks where the high-resolution data actually contribute. Version 4.5.0 (June 2026) holds 1,644 swath surveys covering 12.41% of the global ocean. Golfo Dulce is in the other 87.6%: a GMRT GridServer request over the gulf returns the same grid at resolution=max, high and med, which is the signature of a request being served from the interpolated base rather than from swath data.
verbatim_finding: The current version (GMRT v4.5.0) was released in June 2026 and includes swath data from 1,644 surveys covering 44,896,399 square kilometers or 12.41% of the global ocean.
data_availability: Open web services: GridServer (Esri ASCII, netCDF, GeoTIFF), MaskServer, PointServer, profiles, WMS, and GeoMapApp. Retrieved directly for the gulf on 31 July 2026: GridServer over 8.35-8.80°N, 83.10-83.55°W returned an 822 x 821 grid at 5.4931640625e-04° cells (~61 m), with the topo-mask layer showing land masking only.
caveat: GMRT will resample its base layer to whatever cell size you request, so a ~61 m output grid over Golfo Dulce is not evidence of ~61 m data. Independent analysis of the returned grid for this project found only 2.6% of the gulf resting on real soundings, 0.0-0.1% above 150 m depth, plus artefact clusters reaching -2058 m in a basin the literature puts a little over 200 m deep.

title: El complejo marino-hotelero Cocodrilo Bay tendría impacto ambiental grave en península de Osa y golfo Dulce
summary: The technical critique of the Cocodrilo Bay marina-hotel proposal at Puerto Jiménez, published in the July 2013 Ambientico issue devoted entirely to the question of whether Golfo Dulce could support a marina. It works through the fuel-storage risk (180 000 litres of diesel and petrol stored beside the beach on floating docks), the weakness of the spill contingency planning, the risk of treatment-plant failure and illegal discharge causing faecal contamination, the vessel-traffic and noise impacts on cetacean populations, and — the part usually missing from the formal EIA — the indirect real-estate speculation and water-demand effects, drawing the parallel with the failed El Dorado marina at Golfito.
verbatim_finding: los impactos ambientales de una megamarina como la que proyecta la empresa Cocodrilo en Puerto Jiménez no se limitan a la zona costera o área de influencia directa
data_availability: None; an argued technical commentary citing the project's own EIA and a Contraloría report (DFOE-PGAA-11-2009) on coastal groundwater governance.
caveat: Advocacy-adjacent commentary rather than peer-reviewed analysis, and openly written in opposition to the project. Retrieved as part of the complete Ambientico 235 issue PDF mirrored by the Golfo Dulce Whale Heritage Area, not from the UNA repository.

title: Emprendedores sin tierra: Neoliberalismo, reforma y lucha campesina en Palmar Sur, Osa
container: Anuario Centro de Investigación y Estudios Políticos
summary: What happened to the banana lands after the company left. This action-research study with peasant organisations in Palmar Sur — the old United Fruit district in the Diquís delta, and the location of the Finca 6 World Heritage site — traces the conversion of the Instituto de Desarrollo Agrario into the Instituto de Desarrollo Rural and its land policy. The argument is that the reform manufactures 'entrepreneurial' subjects while dispossessing them: the state now regulates access to land by controlling beneficiaries' economic conduct rather than by handing over titles.
verbatim_finding: the reform promotes the production of an entrepreneurial subjectivity, while consolidating a process of dispossession in which peasants are separated from the land
data_availability: Open access. Action-research with named peasant organisations plus analysis of Costa Rican agrarian-institution policy documents; no deposited dataset.
caveat: Explicitly written from within the peasant organisations' struggle (investigación-acción); it privileges their account and does not present the institutions' case.

title: Spatial and temporal patterns of R. typus in the tropical fjord Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: An interview-plus-survey study (47 interviews, December 2006 – March 2007, plus a repeated transect) that puts numbers on whale shark occurrence in the gulf where direct observation is sparse. Local ecological knowledge yields a maximum of 226 individuals sighted between 2001 and 2007 and a conservative minimum of 190, against zero encounters during the author's own two-and-a-half-month field season. That contrast is itself the finding: whale shark presence in Golfo Dulce is real but strongly pulsed, so short surveys will miss it and interview-based methods are necessary to characterise it.
verbatim_finding: The maximum number of individuals sighted from 2001–2007 was Nmax=226.
data_availability: Interview-derived sighting counts and surface salinity/temperature transect protocol described; underlying interview records held in the author's 2007 MSc thesis.
caveat: Conference proceedings abstract, not a peer-reviewed full paper; the population figures rest on fisher and guide recollection with no correction for double-counting beyond the author's conservative minimum.

title: Racism and Nationalism in the Creation of Costa Rica's Pacific Coast Banana Enclave
summary: The essential account of who was allowed to work the Golfo Dulce banana lands and who was not. Harpelle shows that the 1934 banana contract between the Costa Rican government and the United Fruit Company — the legal instrument that enabled the Pacific enclave at Golfito and Palmar — carried a clause barring 'people of colour' from employment on the Pacific coast, and that the state then moved against the Afro-Caribbean community of Limón by closing English-language schools, pushing farmers off land and deporting West Indians. It explains why the Golfito workforce was demographically unlike Limón's from the outset.
verbatim_finding: the agreement took aim at the West Indian immigrant by prohibiting “people of colour” from working for United Fruit on the Pacific coast
data_availability: None deposited. Archival historical study drawing on Costa Rican government records, the banana contracts and contemporary press; the article is behind the Cambridge University Press paywall.
caveat: Paywalled at Cambridge Core; only the publisher abstract (via Crossref) was retrieved, not the full text. Focus is on race and labour policy, not on Golfito's physical or maritime development.

title: Morphology and sediment structures in Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: This is, as far as this harvest can establish, the only dedicated acoustic survey of the Golfo Dulce sea floor ever published. It was run from R/V Victor Hensen during the 1993/1994 Costa Rica expedition and consists of fourteen sediment-echosounder profiles at 18 kHz — a single-beam, sub-bottom-profiling instrument, not a swath system. It resolves the along-track structure of the inner basin (an oriental fault scarp reaching 170 m of relief, two subordinate parallel faults, turbidite channels feeding the flat basin floor) but by construction it produces lines, not area coverage. Any statement about the shape of the inner basin between those fourteen lines is interpolation. This entry is the answer to 'who measured what, when, with what instrument'.
verbatim_finding: Sediment echosounder records (18 KHz) of 14 profiles were made in the fjord-like embayment of Golfo Dulce.
data_availability: None digitally. The echosounder records are reproduced as figures in the article; no soundings, tracks or grids were archived at NCEI, PANGAEA or GMRT under this cruise as far as could be determined. The article PDF is free at the Revista de Biología Tropical archive.
caveat: Fourteen profile lines over a ~680 km² gulf. Single-beam sub-bottom profiler, not multibeam: it images what is under the ship and nothing to either side. Published in a supplement volume with no DOI, which is part of why it is invisible to most bathymetric data discovery.

title: Morphology and sediment structures in Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: Fourteen 18 kHz echosounder profiles run during the RV Victor Hensen expedition (January 1994), giving the first systematic map of the basin's shape and of the sediment structures on its floor. This is the physical geometry that controls the whole oxygen problem: it documents the ~60 m sill, the >200 m flat inner basin, and a steep NE-side tectonic fault scarp reaching ~170 m of relief. It also shows the flat inner basin is floored by turbidites delivered down channels, leaving most slope sediment undisturbed — relevant because turbidite deposition is later invoked to explain why sulfide does not accumulate.
verbatim_finding: is a fjord-like structure with a deep inner basin (>200 m) sheltered against the open Pacific by a shallow sill (60 m)
data_availability: Echosounder profile tracks and interpreted bathymetric map are reproduced as figures in the PDF. No digital soundings released; the raw 18 kHz records are not archived online.
caveat: Single-beam echosounder along 14 lines only — this is a reconnaissance, not a bathymetric survey. The journal's own DOI for this article does not resolve; cite by URL.

title: Sedimentation in a tropical fjord: Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The only dedicated study of what is actually accumulating on the floor of Golfo Dulce, and the single most important source for the sediment-core question. Surface samples plus 3.5-m gravity/piston cores show the gulf fill is overwhelmingly terrigenous (>90% non-biogenic), with organic carbon and carbonate also arriving from land rather than from the water column, and sourced from different stretches of the surrounding coast. Crucially it reports that the cores contain no laminated intervals, so the Golfo Dulce basin does not behave like the Black Sea or Cariaco Basin as a varve archive despite being periodically anoxic — the record is instead split between turbiditic basin deposits and hemipelagic slope deposits, implying episodic gravity-flow resedimentation into the inner basin.
verbatim_finding: The sediment cores did not show any laminated sections. The sediments can be divided into turbiditic basin deposits and almost undisturbed, hemipelagic slope deposits.
data_availability: No public dataset. Core descriptions, grain-size, organic carbon and carbonate data are presented in the paper's figures and tables only; the full text is behind a Springer paywall.
caveat: Abstract read on the Springer landing page; full text not accessible. Core length (3.5 m) is short, so the record is late Holocene at best and the absence of laminations may not be representative of the deepest anoxic sub-basins.

title: Análisis espacial de los hábitats críticos del delfín nariz de botella (Tursiops truncatus) y la ballena jorobada (Megaptera novaeangliae) en el Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica: Consideraciones acerca de un proyecto de construcción de marina
summary: The peer-reviewed evidence base against the Puerto Jiménez marina proposal, and the only spatial analysis that maps cetacean critical habitat against a specific development footprint in the gulf. Kernel density estimation over 407 bottlenose dolphin records (2005-2014) and 167 humpback whale records (2010-2014) shows dolphin foraging aggregations tied to every major river mouth in the inner basin and around the sill, humpback calving and nursing concentrated on the western sill, and singing males aggregating at the sill centre. The overlap with the proposed marina footprint is the paper's explicit conclusion. Fieldwork by CEIC (Centro de Investigación de Cetáceos Costa Rica), based in Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: valorando los impactos potenciales del desarrollo costero, por un proyecto de marina, al solaparse con hábitats críticos de las especies en estudio
data_availability: Kernel density surfaces and nearest-neighbour statistics are published as figures with parameters reported; the underlying sightings database is held by the research group and is not deposited.
caveat: Effort-based sightings data are not corrected for uneven survey coverage; the marina design assessed is the version circulating at the time of writing.

title: Guerreros del Golfo Dulce: industria forestal y conflicto en la Península de Osa, Costa Rica
container: Departamento Ecuménico de Investigaciones (DEI), San José
summary: The fullest book-length social history of the Osa peninsula in Spanish, built around the 1990s conflict over Ston Forestal's gmelina plantation and chip-export port in Golfo Dulce, but opening with a compact historical review of how the peninsula was settled. It documents the failure of sixteenth- and seventeenth-century Spanish attempts to plant settlements here, the 1840s arrival of chiricano migrants who founded Puerto Jiménez, the state's failed European colonisation schemes aimed at holding the territory against Colombia, the marginal export trade (dried beef, canned lard, coconut oil, pearl shell) that persisted to the 1930s, and United Fruit's 1936 move into the South Pacific. It then reconstructs the AECO campaign, the Agujas evictions and the Greenpeace intervention from local testimony.
verbatim_finding: La Península de Osa siempre tuvo un carácter relativamente aislado. Hubo algunos intentos de poblar el área durante la colonia española, sin embargo la motivación para hacer eso en una zona tan aislada, boscosa y casi sin población indígena, no se dio
data_availability: Full text openly readable and downloadable from the Internet Archive (identifier guerrerosdelgolf00homb, public scan, ~944k characters of OCR); also indexed by the Biodiversity Heritage Library. Ethnographic interview material is presented in the text, not as a deposited corpus.
caveat: Openly partisan in framing — the author writes from within the environmentalist and peasant-movement side of the Ston Forestal conflict. The historical background chapter leans on secondary sources (Lewis 1982/1984, García 1988, Barrantes 1995) that should be checked directly.

title: IHO/OHI Publication C-55: Status of Hydrographic Surveying and Charting Worldwide
summary: The authoritative international register of how well each coastal state's waters are surveyed, and the single hardest number available for this project. The Costa Rica entry (compilation retrieved 31 July 2026) records that for waters shallower than 200 m only 10% is adequately surveyed and 90% requires re-survey; for waters deeper than 200 m the figures are 5% and 95%. Golfo Dulce, at 215 m maximum and with the whole gulf inside the 200 m contour bar the basin floor, falls in the 90%-requires-re-survey category. The notes add that the top national priority is a modern survey of port approaches — that is, not of a remote fjord basin.
verbatim_finding: Top priority is modern survey of the approaches to all ports.
data_availability: Free 528-page trilingual PDF, one page per state, regenerated on request from the IHO C-55 database; per-country figures are supplied by national authorities via an online form. No machine-readable download of the underlying database is offered publicly.
caveat: The Costa Rica page is flagged '(B)' and its own note states 'Percentages provided by USNOO and subject to concurrence of national authority' — the percentages are a US Naval Oceanographic Office estimate, not a Costa Rican measurement. Costa Rica's own 2024 national report says it has no C-55 update to offer.

title: Comunicación de Acuerdo A.J.D.I.P./191-2010: Declarar el Golfo Dulce como Área Marina Para la Pesca Responsable
authors: Junta Directiva del Instituto Costarricense de Pesca y Acuicultura (INCOPESCA)
container: Instituto Costarricense de Pesca y Acuicultura (INCOPESCA)
summary: This is the founding legal instrument of the Área Marina de Pesca Responsable Golfo Dulce — the single most important governance document for the gulf's marine management. Adopted 11 June 2010 in extraordinary session A.J.D.I./39-2010, it establishes the AMPR under the INCOPESCA framework regulation A.J.D.I.P./138-2008 and Executive Decree 35502-MAG (La Gaceta 191, 1 October 2009), approves the accompanying Plan de Ordenamiento Pesquero, and sets the gear restrictions that define what fishing is legal inside the gulf. It also names the seven artisanal and sport-fishing associations that petitioned for the declaration, which is the cleanest available roster of organised fishing stakeholders in Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: Artículo 1. Aprobar el establecimiento del Área Marina Para la Pesca Responsable del Golfo Dulce, conforme a lo establecido en el Reglamento A.J.D.I.P 138-2008 y el Decreto Ejecutivo Nª35502-MAG
data_availability: No datasets. The PDF is the full text of the agreement including the considerandos and articles; the associated zoning is in the separate Plan de Ordenamiento Pesquero.
caveat: An INCOPESCA board agreement, not an executive decree; its legal force derives from Decreto 35502-MAG. Subsequent AJDIP agreements have modified gear rules, so this text is not necessarily the current consolidated regime.
