title: Propuesta de Plan de Ordenamiento Pesquero del Área Marina para la Pesca Responsable Golfo Dulce
authors: Instituto Costarricense de Pesca y Acuicultura (INCOPESCA)
container: Instituto Costarricense de Pesca y Acuicultura (INCOPESCA)
summary: The operative management plan behind the AMPR declaration, and the richest single Spanish-language source on who fishes the gulf and how. It documents the seven petitioning associations one by one (membership, finances, community projects, obstacles), reports household socio-economic survey results from the fishing communities, defines the participatory zoning of the gulf and the permitted gear per zone, and lists the commercial target species. It also states the areas explicitly excluded from AMPR zoning and the pre-existing norms that remain in force, which matters for anyone trying to reconstruct the current legal patchwork.
verbatim_finding: Se han generado impactos en la zona costera (playas, bocas de ríos y aguas litorales) por arrastre intensivo de sedimentos de los ríos principales, producto de la deforestación y mal uso del suelo.
data_availability: Tabulated survey results from fisher households and association profiles are printed in the PDF; the zoning is given as a cartographic sheet. No machine-readable data or GIS layers are distributed.
caveat: Formally a 'propuesta' dated June 2010; parts of the biological framing are secondary and lightly cited. Fifteen years old, so the fisher-association roster and socio-economic figures should be treated as historical.

title: Ordenamiento Espacial Marino: Una Guía de Conceptos y Pasos Metodológicos
summary: MarViva's methodological guide to marine spatial planning for Latin America, and the document that contains the only published multi-use compatibility analysis for Golfo Dulce specifically. Alongside the general method — habitat fragility and use-pressure scoring, pairwise compatibility matrices, scenario construction — it works the southern Pacific of Costa Rica as the running example, with figures for dolphin feeding grounds, shrimp reproduction and shark nursery areas against bottom fishing, a compatibility matrix for the uses occurring in Golfo Dulce, a map of fisheries regulations, and an analysis of conflicts between existing uses and the regulatory framework.
verbatim_finding: esta figura muestra que la pesca de arrastre y el tránsito de grandes embarcaciones son incompatibles con muchos otros usos en el área
data_availability: Compatibility matrices and thematic maps are reproduced as figures in the PDF. Underlying spatial layers are not attached, but MarViva runs a public Geoportal (geoportal.marviva.net) where regional layers are served.
caveat: A methods guide, not a completed marine spatial plan for Golfo Dulce; the gulf appears as a worked illustration, and the compatibility judgements are expert-assigned rather than empirically derived.

title: Island arc response to shallow subduction of the Cocos Ridge, Costa Rica
container: Geological Society of America Special Papers 295
summary: The synthesis that ties the whole southern Costa Rican margin together and supplies the regional-scale reason the coastline here is indented and structurally inverted. Six consequences of shallow Cocos Ridge subduction are identified: a gap in the volcanic arc, shallowing of the subducted slab dip, forearc indentation of the Pacific margin of Costa Rica, structural inversion of both the Térraba forearc and the Limón backarc basins, arching of on- and offshore acoustic basement parallel to convergence, and a radial stress pattern around the underthrust area inferred from earthquake focal mechanisms. Golfo Dulce sits inside the indented, inverted forearc this paper describes.
verbatim_finding: Shallow subduction of the Cocos Ridge beneath the Costa Rican island arc results in six major tectonic effects.
data_availability: Compilation of onshore geology, offshore seismic-reflection profiles and earthquake focal mechanisms, presented as maps and sections. No deposited dataset. GSA paywall.
caveat: Only a truncated abstract was retrievable; the full text is paywalled and was not read. A 1995 synthesis, so superseded in detail by later GPS and seismic work.

title: Tectonic evolution and origin of the Golfo Dulce gold placers in southern Costa Rica
summary: The dissenting account of how the Golfo Dulce region came to look the way it does, and essential for not presenting the pull-apart model as settled. Kriz argues the whole area was a single island from the Early Miocene to the Late Pleistocene, raised by post-Cretaceous anticlinal doming of deep oceanic crust, which then broke apart tectonically between the Late Pleistocene and the present. In his model the present relief is produced by thrusting — the Osa Reverse Fault and the Eastern (Oriental) Golfo Dulce Fault carrying older basement over its own sedimentary cover — rather than by strike-slip extension, and he denies outright that Pliocene pull-apart basins or Panama Fracture Zone-related dextral faults exist here.
verbatim_finding: Therefore, no "pull-apart" Pliocene basins exist in the Golfo Dulce area, nor do certain right-lateral strike-slip faults related to the Panama Fracture Zone.
data_availability: Cross-sections, a stratigraphic model of three gold-enrichment cycles and mapped fault traces are in the paper. Scanned PDF free from the UCR archive; no digital dataset.
caveat: Explicitly contradicts Berrangé (1987, 1989). A minority position; most later literature (Corrigan et al. 1990, Gardner et al. 1992, Vannucchi et al. 2006) favours ridge-subduction-driven uplift with strike-slip and reverse block faulting rather than either end-member. Scanned PDF, no text layer.

title: Microhuellas de manufactura: tecnología lapidaria en la Costa Rica precolombina
summary: Experimental archaeology on how pre-Columbian Costa Rican craftspeople actually worked stone, using digital microscopy (Keyence VHX-5000) to read manufacturing micro-traces on greenstone celtiform pendants and replicating hypothesised lapidary techniques. Its relevance to the spheres is methodological and social: it demonstrates measurable variation in carving technique and difficulty, and argues from that variation for multiple artisan groups of differing social origin rather than a single specialist workshop — the same question that dominates debate over who made and moved the Diquís spheres.
verbatim_finding: Este artículo se enfoca en los aspectos tecnológicos de los colgantes hachaoides de piedras verdes en la Costa Rica precolombina.
data_availability: Open-access HTML, PDF and EPUB, pp. 1–22, with microscope images of manufacturing traces and documentation of the replication experiments. No separate deposited image or measurement dataset.
caveat: Concerns greenstone pendants, not the Diquís spheres, and is national in scope rather than specific to the Osa/Diquís region — supporting evidence on craft organisation, not direct evidence about sphere production.

title: Microbiological observations in the anoxic basin Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The microbiological companion to Thamdrup et al. (1996) from the same Victor Hensen cruise, combining Most-Probable-Number counts, microscopy and molecular techniques on the sulfur-cycling community. It supplies the mechanistic reason why the basin's sulfide stays low: sulfate-reducer numbers peak in and near the sediment rather than through the water column, and free-swimming sulfide oxidisers (Thiovulum, Thiospira) plus vacuolated Beggiatoa occupy the anoxic bottom water and sediment–water interface, consuming sulfide as it is produced.
verbatim_finding: Although no oxygen was present hydrogen sulfide was only detectable close to the sediment.
data_availability: MPN count tables and micrographs published in the article. No sequence accessions or data deposit (predates routine GenBank submission for this kind of survey).
caveat: Cultivation-based (MPN) counts strongly under-represent true abundance; superseded for community composition by later 16S sequencing work, though its sulfur-bacteria observations still stand.

title: Macroinfauna of a tropical fjord-like embayment: Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The most direct empirical statement in the literature of what the anoxic basin does to bottom life. Twenty-six box cores taken by the R/V Victor Hensen in December 1993 at nine stations between 43 and 200 m yielded 1690 individuals in 69 species, overwhelmingly polychaetes, with eight species accounting for 73 % of individuals. Decisively, no organisms at all were recovered from the two deepest (200 m) stations inside the gulf, while a diverse fauna occurred at comparable depths outside the sill and at shallower depths inside. The sill station at 75 m was the most species-rich (37 species), functioning as a transition zone. Comparison with a 1976 survey shows near-complete turnover in species composition at similar diversity, which the authors attribute to fluctuating hypoxia-anoxia plus El Niño forcing.
verbatim_finding: The fluctuating bottom conditions of hypoxia-anoxia characteristic of most of Golfo Dulce, in addition to the likely impact of strong El Niño in the marine ecosystems, might be the causes for drastic shifts in species composition and abundance.
data_availability: Station-by-station species abundance data, diversity and evenness indices, and cluster analyses of the 1976 and 1993 datasets are published in the open-access PDF (Rev. Biol. Trop. 46 Suppl. 6: 81–90).
caveat: No DOI was ever registered for this article, so it is cited here by its stable OJS landing page. Single cruise, three days of sampling, 500 µm mesh — the azoic result at 200 m is a snapshot of one anoxic episode, not a demonstration of permanent lifelessness.

title: Capturas de la raya Dasyatis longa (Myliobatiformes: Dasyatidae) en las pesquerías artesanales de Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: Companion analysis focused on the longtail stingray, the dominant batoid in the artisanal catch (75.7 % of rays, more than 10 % of total catch). Its value here is spatial and bathymetric: it names and ranks the fishing grounds actually used — Los Bajos, Pique Fijo, La Ciénaga, Lapa-Ríos, Piedra del Sombrero, Pavones — and records that these operations take place over muddy bottoms in water shallower than 30 m. That is a concrete statement of where the demersal fishery can physically operate in a basin whose deeper bottom is hypoxic to anoxic, and it complements the depth-distribution evidence from the flatfish and macroinfauna work.
verbatim_finding: We observed a total of 30 artisanal fishing operations in different areas of Golfo Dulce, with muddy bottoms and very shallow waters (less than 30m).
data_availability: Per-ground effort shares, sex ratio, disc-width statistics and monthly CPUE for D. longa are given in the open-access article.
caveat: Same 2010–2011 observer programme as the shark paper, so the two are not independent samples; near-total live release means catch numbers are not landings.

title: Tiburones y rayas capturados por pesquerías artesanales con línea de fondo en el Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: Direct observer-based evidence of what the gulf's legal bottom-longline fishery actually catches, which is the empirical test of whether the AMPR gear regime is protecting elasmobranchs. Across 67 trips between May 2010 and May 2011, split between onboard observation and landing-site monitoring, the authors recorded 609 sharks of ten species — scalloped hammerhead alone over half — plus rays, and documented that 65 sharks and 111 rays were released alive because of low commercial value. CPUE peaks for sharks in July-August and for rays in January-February give a concrete seasonal hook for any temporal closure. The authors run Asociación Conservacionista Misión Tiburón, based in Costa Rica and active in Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: Durante las 67 faenas de pesca se analizaron en total 609 tiburones pertenecientes a diez especies.
data_availability: Species composition, CPUE by month and release outcomes are tabulated in the open-access article. No raw trip-level dataset deposited.
caveat: One year of sampling and only one gear type (bottom longline); it does not cover gillnet or shrimp-trawl bycatch, and is now over a decade old.

title: Conociendo lo invisible de un fiordo tropical: estructura del bacterioplancton en el Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica.
container: ISMEL 2025 — Simposio de Microbiología (Universidad Nacional de Costa Rica)
summary: The first molecular characterisation of the Golfo Dulce bacterioplankton, from a cooperative oceanographic campaign between Costa Rican public institutions, private industry and NASA. Seven stations were sampled from coastal waters out to the most oceanic point of the gulf; 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (Illumina MiSeq) was paired with environmental (temperature, salinity) and inorganic-nutrient measurements. The reported result is a strong correlation between bacterioplankton distribution and the physicochemical variables, with Cyanobacteria, Rhodobacterales and some Bacteroidetes shifting in composition along the coast-to-ocean transect — the microbial community structure that older cultivation-based work (Kuever et al. 1996) could not resolve.
verbatim_finding: En el mundo existen únicamente cuatro fiordos tropicales, y el Golfo Dulce, ubicado en el Pacífico sur de Costa Rica, es uno de ellos.
data_availability: Conference abstract only; no sequence accessions, station coordinates or environmental data released with it. Contact carolina.marin.vindas@una.cr (Universidad Nacional, Escuela de Ciencias Biológicas) for the underlying data.
caveat: Conference abstract, not a peer-reviewed paper — roughly 300 words with no figures, tables or methods detail beyond the platform used. Treat all findings as provisional pending full publication.

title: Museos comunitarios en Boruca y Curré/Yimba, Costa Rica: desarrollo reciente, participación comunitaria y autodeterminación
summary: Documents how the two Brunca (Boruca) communities of Boruca and Curré/Yimba run their own community museums as instruments of self-determination rather than as heritage display. Based on interviews with the museum working committees, it analyses three dimensions — the concept of a community museum, learning and coexistence, and communal historical memory — and positions the museums as alternative spaces for managing memory and culture. This is the clearest published account of how the Brunca themselves curate their own past in the region immediately inland of Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: El objetivo del artículo es posicionar el quehacer de los museos comunitarios en los territorios indígenas de Boruca y Curré/Yimba, en Costa Rica, como actores claves en los proyectos de desarrollo comunitario y profundamente vinculados con la vida comunal.
data_availability: Qualitative interview study with members of the museum committees; findings reported narratively. No deposited dataset.
caveat: The UNED journal platform (revistas.uned.ac.cr) is behind a bot-detection wall and could not be opened directly; metadata and the quoted abstract were retrieved from the Crossref record. Verify page numbers against the publisher PDF before citing.

title: Influence of Incoming Plate Relief on Overriding Plate Deformation and Earthquake Nucleation: Cocos Ridge Subduction (Costa Rica)
summary: Images the crust directly beneath and seaward of the Osa margin with a 2D P-wave velocity model plus a coincident multichannel seismic reflection profile, and connects that structure to the 2002 Osa earthquake sequence — the closest large event to Golfo Dulce in the instrumental record. The overriding plate is divided into three domains from imbricate thin-skinned thrusting at the trench, through landward-dipping reflector packages and actively deforming shelf sediment, to a little-fractured domain beneath ~2 km of landward-dipping strata; the bulk of the margin is highly consolidated rock and its uplift is attributed to thick-skinned tectonics. Oceanic crustal thickness falls from ~14 km at the trench (Cocos Ridge) to 6–7 km beneath the shelf.
verbatim_finding: The 2002 Osa sequence nucleated at the leading flank of subducting seamounts in the area of highest tectonic overpressure.
data_availability: Wide-angle seismic tomography model, multichannel seismic profile and derived stress/strain models presented in the paper. Free (bronze OA) PDF at onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1029/2019TC005586. Underlying seismic data from the CRISP/BGR surveys.
caveat: A single 2D transect offshore Osa; results are not directly constrained inside Golfo Dulce, and a 2020 EGU abstract version of the same work exists (10.5194/egusphere-egu2020-2940).

title: Dimensión Humana de los Ecosistemas Marinos de la Región de Osa y Golfito
container: INOGO, Stanford Woods Institute for the Environment, Stanford University
summary: The marine-ecosystem volume of the Iniciativa Osa y Golfito (INOGO), a Stanford-led regional planning effort that produced the most systematic recent synthesis of how people use the gulf and what that use costs. It moves from biogeography and habitat description through ecosystem services to the pressures — water quality, land-use legacies, resource-extraction practices — and frames the region's marine ecosystems as already in a state of danger despite low population density. Because INOGO was designed as an input to regional development planning rather than as academic output, it is the closest thing available to a marine spatial-planning baseline for Osa and Golfito.
verbatim_finding: Los ecosistemas marinos de la región de Osa y Golfito proporcionan gran diversidad biológica, así como un gran conjunto de servicios ecosistémicos de los cuáles dependen diferentes usos tradicionales y novedosos.
data_availability: Synthesises published and grey literature with maps of the INOGO study region; compiled tables are in the PDF. No primary dataset released with the report.
caveat: INOGO wound down after its planning phase, so the initiative itself is no longer an active institution; the report's boundary definition is explicitly provisional. Retrieved from the golfodulce.org mirror.

title: Seasonal vertical distribution, abundance, biomass, and biometrical relationships of ostracods in Golfo Dulce, Pacific coast of Costa Rica
summary: Day-and-night stratified Nansen-net sampling (0–20, 20–50, 50–100 m) over 24-hour cycles in May and September 1995, paired with oxygen, temperature and salinity profiles. It is the finest-grained account of how far down the gulf's plankton actually goes: two dominant ostracod species, Cypridina americana and Euchonchoecia chierchiae, were overwhelmingly confined to the upper 20 m, with only 2 % and 0.4 % of individuals respectively below 50 m, and early developmental stages essentially never left the surface layer. Diel vertical migration is therefore truncated in this basin compared with the open ocean. The authors also note that ostracod abundance in Golfo Dulce is extraordinarily high for a system with oceanic affinities, and assign the two species distinct trophic roles (detritivore/facultative predator versus grazer on organic matter).
verbatim_finding: both species were primarily found at depths within the first 20m in May, while at depths greater than 50m abundance was only 2% and 0.4% for C. americana and E. chierchiae, respectively
data_availability: Abundance and dry-weight biomass by developmental stage, layer and time of day, plus length–weight biometric relationships, are tabulated in the open-access PDF (Rev. Biol. Trop. 56 Suppl. 4: 125–147).
caveat: The journal page advertises DOI 10.15517/rbt.v56i4.27217 but it is not registered with Crossref (HTTP 404), so this is cited by URL. Two sampling campaigns in a single year (1995); the authors attribute the shallow distribution primarily to predator avoidance and food resources rather than oxygen, so the oxygen interpretation is ours to make carefully.

title: La diversidad marina del Golfo Dulce, Pacífico sur de Costa Rica: amenazas a su conservación
summary: The standard Spanish-language statement of what is at stake in Golfo Dulce and what threatens it, written by the CIMAR/UCR researcher who has led most of the gulf's oceanographic work. It compiles 1 028 marine species from the literature — 21.5% of the 4 745 reported for Costa Rica's entire Pacific coast — and normalises this against coastline length and area to show that the gulf carries more than double the per-km² species density of Golfo de Nicoya for macrocrustaceans, molluscs, marine worms, plankton and fish. It then names the threat set (agriculture, deforestation, sediment, coastal contamination, development projects) and argues for integrated management.
verbatim_finding: Esta extraordinaria biodiversidad es amenazada por actividades agrícolas, deforestación, sedimentos y diferentes tipos de contaminación costera, así como por el desarrollo de diversos proyectos.
data_availability: Species counts and diversity indices per taxonomic group are tabulated in the article; underlying species lists are drawn from the cited literature, not deposited. Full text PDF is openly downloadable.
caveat: A review/compilation, not primary survey work; the species total is a literature tally and is sensitive to uneven sampling effort across taxa. The UNED journal site sits behind bot mitigation — the full text was read from an open mirror copy of the same article PDF.

title: Rasgos oceanográficos en el Golfo Dulce, Pacífico de Costa Rica: una revisión para la toma de decisiones en conservación marina
summary: The opening synthesis of the 2015 Golfo Dulce supplement, combining meteorology, circulation, nutrient chemistry and zooplankton from 2005–2007 surveys into a single conservation-facing picture. For the ecological question it supplies the measured oxygen numbers that everything else must be read against: deep water between 70 and 140 m was not wholly devoid of oxygen during this period but held only 0.25–1.10 mg/L, and nitrate enrichment at depth records the decomposition of sinking organic matter. Copepods made up 44–83.6 % of zooplankton. The authors combine this with fjord-type circulation (surface currents ~18 cm/s near the sill decaying inward to ~5 cm/s) to argue for zoning of human activities in the gulf.
verbatim_finding: Dissolved oxygen was not absent in deep waters (70m to 140m), but concentrations were low (0.25mg/L to 1.10mg/L).
data_availability: Current speeds, nutrient and dissolved-oxygen profiles, zooplankton composition, wave heights and rainfall series for 2005–2007 are presented in the open-access article; raw CTD data not deposited.
caveat: Sampling stopped at 140 m and one station was visited only once, so the deepest, most persistently anoxic water (below ~150 m) is not represented; the 'not absent' oxygen finding therefore describes the oxycline, not the basin floor, and does not contradict reports of anoxia at 200 m.

title: Quaternary outer fore-arc deformation and uplift inboard of the Panama Triple Junction, Burica Peninsula
container: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
summary: Documents the Panama Triple Junction (Cocos–Nazca–Caribbean) migrating southeastward past the Golfo Dulce system at roughly 55 mm/yr, and what that does to the peninsula forming the gulf's southeastern wall. Burica is shown to be dominated by contractional deformation on three listric thrusts rooting into the plate boundary, driven by the eastward migration of the Cocos Ridge flank rather than by changes in convergence rate or obliquity. Eight marine terraces are mapped and dated by radiocarbon, OSL and soil chronosequences; the easternmost terraces range from Marine Isotope Stage 3 to Holocene, meaning that part of the peninsula is younger than ~60 ka. This is the clearest regional demonstration that the land around Golfo Dulce is emerging fast enough to have reorganised the coastline within the last glacial cycle.
verbatim_finding: Time-averaged uplift rates calculated from marine terraces and other Quaternary marine deposits yield consistent uplift rates that range between 2.1 ± 0.1 and 7.7 ± 0.5 mm/yr for samples older than 1 ka
data_availability: Terrace inner-edge elevation surveys, 14C and OSL ages, soil chronosequence data and balanced cross sections are in the paper and its auxiliary material. AGU/Wiley paywall.
caveat: The very high rates derived from samples younger than 1 ka (6.9–19.3 mm/yr) are interpreted by the authors as not yet averaged over a full seismic cycle and should not be read as long-term rates.

title: Apparent stress variations near the Osa Peninsula, Costa Rica, influenced by subducted bathymetric features
summary: Seismological evidence that the subducted seamounts and ridge topography beneath the Osa region concentrate stress on the plate interface. Apparent stress is computed by seismic coda methods for 114 aftershocks (0.9 ≤ ML ≤ 3.7) of the 1999 Mw 6.9 Quepos thrust earthquake, giving a heterogeneous distribution of 0.1–2.5 MPa with a mean of 0.6 MPa — more than twice the global mean for thrust earthquakes at oceanic subduction zones and 1.5 times the mean measured along the same margin near Nicoya, where the incoming plate has lower relief. Source scaling is constant. Supports the recurring theme that the roughness of the incoming Cocos plate, not just convergence rate, governs both deformation and seismicity around Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: The variation in apparent stress found near the Osa Peninsula, and high mean as compared to global and regional values, suggest areas of stress concentration in the region of bathymetric complexity in the subduction zone.
data_availability: Derived apparent-stress values for 114 aftershocks are given in the paper and its auxiliary material; source waveforms are from temporary and permanent regional networks. Free (bronze OA) PDF at onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1029/2010GL045955.
caveat: Aftershocks are small (ML ≤ 3.7) and belong to a single 1999 sequence centred near Quepos, some distance northwest of Golfo Dulce; extrapolation to the gulf itself is indirect.

title: Naufragios en Costa Rica: barcos históricos representantes del patrimonio cultural subacuático
container: Museo Nacional de Costa Rica, Artículos Educativos
summary: The national inventory of investigated historic wrecks, and therefore the source that settles — negatively — the question of submerged archaeology in Golfo Dulce. The Museo Nacional lists eight vessels whose remains it has investigated: Pecio San Lucas-1, -2 and -3 in the Golfo de Nicoya near playa El Inglés; the Punta Cahuita monument on the Caribbean, in two sectors (anchors-and-cannons, and bricks); and Pecio Manzanillo-1 and -2 on the southern Caribbean coast. None is in Golfo Dulce, on the Osa coast or anywhere in the southern Pacific. The page also records that Costa Rica ratified the 2001 UNESCO underwater-heritage convention in 2018, and notes the general pattern that most sinkings occur in bays near port cities and anchorages.
verbatim_finding: Tal fue el destino de ocho embarcaciones que naufragaron en aguas costarricenses, cuyos restos han sido investigados por el Museo Nacional.
data_availability: Descriptive site-by-site summaries with photographs and estimated dimensions. Formal records sit in the national underwater cultural heritage register (Ley 9500 and its 2022 regulation); the museum invites coastal communities to report sites, so the register is explicitly incomplete.
caveat: Undated outreach page with no named author, and it is an inventory of what has been investigated, not of what exists. Absence of Golfo Dulce here is evidence of no survey, not evidence of no wrecks — and given the gulf's anoxic bottom water, an unsurveyed basin is exactly where organic hull material would survive.

title: NCEI Multibeam Bathymetry Database and IHO Data Centre for Digital Bathymetry (Seafloor Mapping)
authors: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
IHO Data Centre for Digital Bathymetry
container: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
summary: The world's public archive of ship multibeam, and the decisive negative result for this topic. Querying its survey-footprint service directly on 31 July 2026 for the inner basin (83.45-83.15°W, 8.55-8.75°N) returns zero surveys. Widening to the whole gulf and its mouth returns exactly three, all deep-ocean transits that pass offshore and never enter the gulf: ARIA02WT (R/V Thomas Washington, 1982, SeaBeam), NEMO03MV (R/V Melville, 2000, SeaBeam 2000) and DANA02RR (R/V Roger Revelle, 2003, Simrad EM120). Checking their track coordinates confirms none has a single vertex inside the gulf. No multibeam echosounder has ever been run inside Golfo Dulce and archived publicly.
verbatim_finding: NCEI and the IHO Data Center for Digital Bathymetry (DCDB) archive and share depth data acquired by hydrographic, oceanographic, and industry vessels and platforms during surveys or while on passage.
data_availability: Free and unrestricted. Queried via the ArcGIS REST endpoint gis.ngdc.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/web_mercator/multibeam_dynamic/MapServer/0/query with an esriGeometryEnvelope in EPSG:4326; results reproducible. Raw sonar files and derived grids are downloadable per survey.
caveat: Absence from NCEI is not absolute absence: a national, naval or commercial survey held privately would not appear. But NCEI is the IHO's designated global data centre, so anything intended for public or charting use should be here.

title: NCEI Marine Trackline Geophysical Data (single-beam bathymetry, sub-bottom and seismic)
authors: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
container: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
summary: The companion archive that closes off the pre-multibeam era, covering single-beam bathymetry, sub-bottom profiles and seismic reflection from 1939 to the present with worldwide coverage. Queried on 31 July 2026, the inner-basin envelope returns zero bathymetry tracks and zero multichannel seismic lines. Widening to the whole gulf returns three Scripps deep-ocean transits — PAPA02BD (R/V Spencer F. Baird, 1965), ARIA02WT (1982) and NEMO03MV (2000) — whose bounding boxes span thousands of kilometres of open Pacific. So there is no archived single-beam sounding line inside Golfo Dulce either, and no seismic profile from which sediment thickness or basement depth could be read.
verbatim_finding: NCEI's Marine Trackline Geophysical database provides single-beam bathymetry, subbottom profiles, magnetic, gravity, side-scan sonar and historic seismic reflection and refraction data collected during marine cruises from 1939–present.
data_availability: Free; exportable in MGD77T. Queried via gis.ngdc.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/web_mercator/trackline_combined_dynamic/MapServer layers 1 (Bathymetry) and 4 (Multi-Channel Seismics) with the same envelopes as the multibeam query.
caveat: Coverage is strongest for US and allied academic cruises; small-boat or national surveys never submitted to NCEI are invisible to this query. The Victor Hensen 1993/94 echosounder lines of Hebbeln et al. are a case in point — they exist in print but not in this archive.

title: NGA Nautical Chart 21562: Golfo Dulce
summary: The only nautical chart dedicated to Golfo Dulce, and a direct measure of the charting vintage. Edition 14 is dated 14 February 1998 at a scale of 1:72,990, last corrected by Notice to Mariners 18 of 1998 — nearly three decades stale. At that scale one millimetre on the paper is 73 m on the water, so the chart cannot represent basin-floor structure at all; it is a navigational document showing enough soundings to keep a hull off the bottom. NGA has since cancelled the chart and no longer serves it for viewing, meaning the best-scale published chart of the gulf is both obsolete and withdrawn.
verbatim_finding: Scale: 72990 Actual Chart Size: 27.2" x 33.1" Paper Size: 36.0" x 35.0" Edition #: 14 Edition Date: 1998-02-14 NTM Notice/Date: 199818 None
data_availability: Print-on-demand paper only via commercial agents; NGA no longer serves the raster image ('charts in this region cannot be viewed'). No digital soundings, no ENC, no source-survey diagram accessible.
caveat: Metadata retrieved from a commercial print agent rather than from NGA directly, because NGA has cancelled and withdrawn the chart. The chart's own source-survey diagram — which would date the underlying soundings — could not be inspected.

title: Diversidad de cetáceos en el paisaje marino costeros de Golfo Dulce, Península de Osa, Costa Rica
summary: The backbone survey for cetacean community structure in the gulf: 943 sightings of 12 species over ten years (2005–2014), 3490 hours and 64533 km of effort. Its contribution is showing that the cetacean assemblage is spatially ordered along the same inner-basin/sill/outer gradient that governs the gulf's hydrography — coastal bottlenose and spotted dolphins in the inner basin, bottlenose plus migratory humpbacks at the sill, and the most diverse, oceanic, piscivorous delphinids in the transitional water outside. It also raises the hypothesis of a resident Golfo Dulce morphotype of pantropical spotted dolphin distinct from S. attenuata graffmani outside.
verbatim_finding: A gradient of cetacean diversity is observed from the inner basin to the transitional-oceanic area at the entrance of the Gulf, with coastal bottlenose dolphin and spotted dolphin dominating the inner basin
data_availability: Sighting counts by species and by seascape unit are tabulated in the open-access PDF; raw positions not deposited.
caveat: The proposed distinct inner-gulf spotted dolphin morphotype is explicitly framed as a hypothesis, not a result. Part of the Golfo Dulce special supplement, Rev. Biol. Trop. 63(S1).

title: Population size and demographic parameters of pantropical spotted dolphin (Stenella attenuata graffmani) (Cetartiodactyla: Delphinidae) in Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The first capture–recapture abundance estimate for the coastal pantropical spotted dolphin inside Golfo Dulce: 280 photo-identified individuals yielding a population of roughly 187–368 animals with very high apparent survival (0.98). Its ecological significance for this project is the finding that a subset of individuals is repeatedly recaptured inside the gulf and concentrates in the inner basin, while 65 % of identified animals were seen only once — evidence of an open population with a resident core that treats the shallow inner basin as critical foraging habitat. The authors argue this core should be managed as an ecologically discrete unit.
verbatim_finding: This group of dolphins appears to favor the inner basin as a critical foraging habitat.
data_availability: Photo-identification catalogue underpins the analysis; model outputs (30 candidate models, QAICc ranking, abundance and survival estimates with CIs) are tabulated in the open-access article.
caveat: Non-random boat surveys and a high proportion of single-sighting individuals mean abundance depends strongly on the emigration scenario assumed; the two parsimonious models give substantially different totals.

title: Agregaciones de alimentación del tiburón ballena, Rhincodon typus (Orectolobiformes: Rhincodontidae) en Golfo Dulce, Península de Osa, Costa Rica
summary: First documentation of whale shark feeding aggregations inside Golfo Dulce — four events between 2009 and 2013, all on the northwestern shore of the inner basin near the Rincón and Tigre river mouths, with a roughly even mix of adults and juveniles. The mechanistic point is that the aggregations sit where terrestrial organic input fertilises the zooplankton community, and calanoid copepods were observed in the water alongside feeding sharks. This makes the world's largest fish an indicator of the gulf's river-fed surface productivity, and directly links land-use in the Osa catchments to a charismatic pelagic species.
verbatim_finding: For the first time, four whale shark feeding aggregations are documented in Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica, a tropical fjord-like embayment located in the south Pacific region of the country.
data_availability: Dates, locations and estimated group structure of the four aggregation events are reported in the open-access article; no photo-ID catalogue published.
caveat: Four opportunistic observations over four years; prey identification is by direct observation of copepods in the water, not by gut content or plankton sampling.

title: Peces arrecifales someros en el islote rocoso La Viuda, Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: Quarterly Bohnsack-and-Bannerot visual censuses through 2002 at the La Viuda rocky islet (8°37'33" N, 83°14'08" W), the only published fish-community time series for a hard-substrate site inside the gulf. Twenty-eight species were recorded, dominated by Pomacentridae and Labridae, with Shannon diversity of 1.1–1.73 nits/ind. The two structuring factors identified — season and wave exposure, with higher diversity in the dry season and on wave-sheltered aspects — give a shallow-water counterpart to the depth-and-oxygen structuring that governs the deeper fauna.
verbatim_finding: I identified 28 species and the most abundant families were Pomacentridae and Labridae.
data_availability: Species list with per-census abundances and diversity indices in the open-access article.
caveat: Single islet, four censuses in one year, single observer — a baseline rather than a monitoring programme.

title: Habitat use of south-eastern Pacific humpback whales (Megaptera novaeangliae; Borowski 1781) in Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: A decade of effort-corrected sighting data (June–October, 2010–2019) resolving how the southeastern Pacific (Southern Hemisphere) humpback population partitions Golfo Dulce internally. The key result is a depth-driven segregation: mother–calf dyads occupy shallow water, where resting and nursing dominate, while adult-only groups use deeper water. This is the paper that converts the gulf's bathymetry into a whale-conservation argument — the shallow inner and marginal waters are nursery habitat and are exactly where boat traffic concentrates — and it is the best-quantified account of humpback habitat use specific to Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: The mother–calf groups were present in waters <80 m deep, and their main behaviour was resting (nursing and social).
data_availability: Sightings-per-unit-effort surfaces, group-composition classifications and behavioural budgets are presented in figures and tables; underlying sighting positions are not deposited in an open repository.
caveat: The publisher landing page (connectsci.au / publish.csiro.au) returned HTTP 403; the abstract quoted here is the publisher's own abstract as deposited with Crossref. Non-random, boat-based survey effort — spatial coverage is uneven.

title: El terremoto del 29 de mayo de 1879: Una ruptura de magnitud Ms ≥ 7,0 en la zona limítrofe sur de Costa Rica y Panamá
summary: Recovers a large forgotten earthquake on the Golfo Dulce shoreline from archival macroseismic evidence, extending the region's seismic record back into the nineteenth century. Damage reports place Modified Mercalli VII–VIII at Santo Domingo, San José (de Golfito) and David — settlements on the southern and northern sides of Golfo Dulce — with MM V–VI felt across central Costa Rica. The intensity pattern matches that of the 3 April 1983 Osa (Ms 7.2) and 18 July 1934 Armuelles (Ms 7.5) events, from which the authors infer a rupture of Ms ≥ 7.0 on one of three candidate sources: the Osa interplate seismogenic zone, the Longitudinal Fault, or the Panama Fracture Zone. Establishes that the gulf sits on a source capable of repeated M7+ ruptures.
verbatim_finding: se concluye que el terremoto de 1879 corresponde con una ruptura de magnitud > 7,0, que puede relacionarse con la zona sísmica interplaca de Osa, con la Falla Longitudinal o con la Zona de Fractura de Panamá
data_availability: Transcribed archival accounts, an intensity table and isoseismal maps are given in the paper. Machine-readable PDF freely downloadable from the UCR archive.
caveat: Magnitude and source are inferred from sparse historical damage reports in a very thinly populated nineteenth-century region; the authors are explicit that the causative fault cannot be resolved among the three candidates.

title: Los ecosistemas marinos del Pacífico sur de Costa Rica: estado del conocimiento y perspectivas de manejo
summary: The standard Spanish-language review of what is known about the southern Pacific of Costa Rica, and therefore the clearest window on how the gulf's morphological numbers propagate. It fixes the canonical figures — inner basin 215 m maximum, sill 60 m, area ~680 km² — and attributes them to Cortés (1990), Córdoba & Vargas (1996) and Hebbeln et al. (1996), i.e. to reef mapping, a station-based hydrographic study and the fourteen echosounder lines. It also carries the only Spanish-language statement of sediment thickness in the gulf, again sourced from the Victor Hensen echosounder records. Its own conclusion is that circulation and deep-water/soft-sediment characterisation remain unstudied.
verbatim_finding: se caracteriza por poseer una cuenca interna de pendiente pronunciada con una profundidad máxima de 215 m y un umbral poco profundo (60 m) a su entrada
data_availability: Review article; no primary data. Free PDF from the Revista de Biología Tropical supplement archive. Its value here is the citation chain it exposes for each morphological number.
caveat: Secondary source. Every depth in it is inherited; the review adds no new measurement and does not question the age or coverage of the underlying surveys.

title: Comportamiento de las masas de agua en el Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica durante El Niño (1997-1998)
summary: The only sustained time series of the Golfo Dulce water column: five stations visited monthly for two years spanning the strong 1997–1998 El Niño, with vertical profiles of temperature, salinity and dissolved oxygen. This is the source for seasonality and interannual variability — it separates inner-basin from outer-gulf hydrography and, most usefully, identifies twice-yearly intrusions of cold, saline, oxygen-rich Pacific water into the basin, tentatively linked to the same forcing that drives Gulf of Panama upwelling. That gives the renewal mechanism a periodicity and a regional driver rather than leaving it as 'erratic'.
verbatim_finding: Finally, biannual events in the influx of cold, high salinity, and oxygen rich oceanic water masses into the basin were detected.
data_availability: Monthly T/S/O2 profiles are shown as contoured sections and figures in the article. No digital deposit; underlying CTD/bottle data held at CIMAR-UCR.
caveat: Spanish text with English abstract. The two years sampled were dominated by an exceptionally strong ENSO event, so the 'normal' seasonal cycle is hard to separate from the anomaly. Journal DOI does not resolve.

title: Posible efecto de El Niño en el zooplancton no gelatinoso del Golfo Dulce, Pacífico de Costa Rica, 1997-1998
summary: Stratified zooplankton sampling at five stations during the 1997–1998 El Niño, with hauls taken deliberately above, through and below the thermocline and paired with Niskin-bottle profiles of temperature, salinity and dissolved oxygen every 10 m. The result is the cleanest published demonstration that the gulf's plankton is vertically compressed: mean abundance was 3793 ind/m3 overall but significantly concentrated in the upper layer at every station (up to 9921 ind/m3), with intermediate densities through the thermocline and a markedly impoverished deep layer. Copepods dominated (71.5 %), followed by appendicularians and ostracods, and inner stations behaved differently from outer ones.
verbatim_finding: The deep layer was relatively poor in zooplankton, with values that varied between 946 ± 1 069 ind/m3 and 1 307 ± 1 270 ind/m3.
data_availability: Abundance by layer and station, taxonomic composition percentages and accompanying hydrographic profiles are published in the open-access PDF (Rev. Biol. Trop. 54 Suppl. 1: 225–240).
caveat: The journal page advertises DOI 10.15517/rbt.v54i1.26833 but that DOI is not registered with Crossref (HTTP 404), so the entry is cited by URL. Sampling stopped at 60–100 m and did not reach the anoxic basin floor, and the study period coincides with a strong El Niño, so it is not a baseline year.

title: Annotated List of Wetlands of International Importance — Costa Rica (Ramsar Sites Information Service)
summary: The authoritative record of Costa Rica's twelve Ramsar sites, and the primary citation for the Térraba-Sierpe designation immediately northwest of Golfo Dulce. It gives site number 782, designation date 11 December 1995, an area of 30 654 ha at 08°52'N 083°36'W, and describes the site as the estuary of two rivers with adjacent lagoons, periodically inundated mangrove and yolillo palm swamp forest, sandy beaches and cliffs, supporting 55 fish species plus commercial shellfish. Crucially for governance it records the human activities recognised inside the site — mangrove extraction for fuel and tannins, traditional fishing, clam and crab harvesting — which is the legal basis of the piangüero economy.
verbatim_finding: Terraba-Sierpe. 11/12/95; Puntarenas; 30,654 ha; 08°52'N 083°36'W. Forest Reserve, National Wetland. The estuary of two rivers, adjacent lagoons, periodically inundated mangrove and "yolillo" palm swamp forest, sandy beaches and cliffs.
data_availability: Site boundaries, areas and coordinates for all twelve Costa Rican Ramsar sites in a downloadable PDF export; full Ramsar Information Sheets and GIS boundaries are served from rsis.ramsar.org per site.
caveat: The export itself is undated and regenerated on request — the year given here is the Térraba-Sierpe designation date, not a publication date. Annotations note 'Most recent RIS information: 1996' for several sites, so descriptions can be badly out of date. The interactive RSIS site pages are behind bot mitigation and could not be read directly.

title: Southern Hemisphere humpback whales wintering off Central America: insights from water temperature into the longest mammalian migration
summary: The quantitative documentation of the dual-hemisphere phenomenon that makes Costa Rican Pacific waters, Golfo Dulce included, unusual among humpback wintering grounds. Photo-identification matches proved that individual whales from Antarctic feeding grounds travel roughly 8300 km to winter off Central America — the longest documented mammalian migration — and that they occupy the same waters that a North Pacific population uses six months earlier or later. The paper also proposes the mechanism: an equatorial tongue of cold water in the eastern South Pacific pushes the Southern Hemisphere wintering ground abnormally far north, and wintering grounds worldwide track a 21.1–28.3 °C water-temperature envelope rather than a latitude.
verbatim_finding: in an area also used by a boreal population during the opposite winter season, resulting in unique spatial overlap between Northern and Southern Hemisphere populations
data_availability: Seven individually photo-identified whales matched between Antarctic and Central American catalogues; wintering-ground positions and sea-surface temperatures are tabulated in the paper. Abstract retrievable free via Europe PMC (PMC2390682); full text paywalled.
caveat: Royal Society landing page returned HTTP 403; the abstract quoted here was retrieved from the Europe PMC record for the same DOI. The overlap is documented for Pacific Costa Rica broadly (whales as far north as ~11°N), not solely for Golfo Dulce; only seven matched individuals underpin the migration claim.

title: Percepción del cambio en la calidad ambiental del paisaje cultural: la ciudad bananera de Golfito, Costa Rica
summary: Treats Golfito as a cultural landscape and asks the people who watched it change what they think was lost. Twenty residents aged 82–94 — old enough to remember the company town at work — were interviewed openly about landscape quality. The finding is that local identity rests jointly on the natural frame (the sea and the mountains that hem the town against its bay) and on the twentieth-century 'banana' infrastructure itself, which the authors treat as heritage rather than as industrial residue. It is a rare piece of documented oral memory of the Golfito waterfront.
verbatim_finding: los aspectos que dan identidad al paisaje local y relevancia a su conservación son la presencia de la naturaleza (representada por el mar y las montañas), y la infraestructura ¨bananera¨ construida en el siglo 20
data_availability: Open-access PDF and HTML. Reports results of an open survey of 20 elderly residents; individual responses are not deposited. A companion English-language paper by the same authors (10.22458/urj.v8i1.1227) adds a 106-photograph comparative landscape analysis.
caveat: Very small purposive sample (n=20) in a single town; perceptions are self-reported and retrospective, so this is testimony rather than measurement.

title: CHEMICAL AND PHYSICAL OBSERVATIONS IN GOLFO, DULCE, AN ANOXIC BASIN ON THE PACIFIC COAST OF COSTA RICA
summary: The founding hydrographic description of Golfo Dulce, based on two occupations of the basin eight days apart in March 1969. It established the basic template every later study works against: a ~200 m inner basin behind a ~60 m sill, oxygen falling to near zero below the pycnocline, nitrate consumed by denitrification below it, and only trace hydrogen sulfide near the bottom. Crucially, the two closely spaced surveys caught a renewal event in progress, which led Richards and colleagues to argue that the basin is flushed erratically rather than being permanently stagnant like Cariaco or Framvaren — the single most important structural fact about this water column.
verbatim_finding: Hydrographic data taken 8 days apart indicated an influx of ocean water into the basin. It appears from past observations in the eastern tropical Pacific that the basin erratically receives ocean water during winter and spring.
data_availability: No modern data deposit. Profile data (temperature, salinity, O2, NO3, NO2, NH4, PO4, SiO4, H2S) are published as tables and figures within the paper itself; the underlying 1969 cruise data are not online.
caveat: Two station occupations in a single month of one year. Everything about seasonality and interannual variation in this paper is inference, not observation.

title: Hidrografía y plumas estuarinas en Golfo Dulce, Pacífico Sur de Costa Rica
summary: A 33-station CTD campaign (2009-2010) whose introduction is the sharpest available evidence that the sill depth is genuinely unconstrained: it states the sill is shallower than 30 m, citing Richards et al. 1971, while Svendsen et al. 2006 — cited two sentences later in the same paragraph for the tidal range — give about 60 m. Both figures circulate simultaneously in the peer-reviewed Spanish literature on the same gulf. The paper also inherits the 215 m inner-basin / 70 m outer-basin split from Wolff, Hartmann & Koch (1996), a trophic modelling paper, which is a striking provenance for a bathymetric statement.
verbatim_finding: Un umbral o silla con menos de 30m ubicado en su entrada restringe la circulación y hace más lenta la renovación del agua en las capas profundas favoreciendo condiciones anóxicas en el fondo
data_availability: CTD profiles, Secchi and chlorophyll-a measurements at 33 stations, presented as figures and sections; no archived data files. Open-access full text at SciELO Costa Rica and revistas.ucr.ac.cr.
caveat: The two sill depths in circulation (<30 m here, ~60 m in Svendsen et al. 2006) differ by a factor of two and neither traces to a survey line across the sill. The CTD in January 2009 reached only 66 m, so this campaign did not itself sound the deep basin.

title: Geomorfología, zonas de erosión y sedimentación costera de la Península de Burica, Costa Rica
summary: Field geomorphological mapping of the western Burica Peninsula, the uplifted block on the Panamanian side of the Golfo Dulce system, from Punta Banco to Punta El Mangle. Landforms are shown to be dominated by structural (fault-controlled) morphologies, with marine, fluvial and denudational forms subordinate — the same signature of tectonic control that Alvarado (1991) reports on the Golfito side. Four coastal erosion–sedimentation zones are delimited (intense erosion; moderate to slight erosion; mixed erosion and sedimentation; depositional). Part of the Revista de Biología Tropical Golfo Dulce special issue, and one of very few Spanish-language field studies of the Quaternary coastal geology of this specific coastline.
verbatim_finding: Los procesos geológicos más importantes son los deslizamientos, la erosión costera y la alta sismicidad del área
data_availability: Geomorphological map and coastal erosion–sedimentation zonation derived from nine days of fieldwork (January 2008), presented as figures in the article. Open-access HTML and PDF at revistas.ucr.ac.cr.
caveat: Based on a single nine-day field campaign covering only the western side of the peninsula; the author notes only part of the wider geological study is reported here.

title: El supuesto determinismo de los cantones bananeros: el cantón Osa, Zona Sur, Costa Rica
summary: Directly challenges the standard narrative that the banana enclave alone explains why the Osa canton is poor. Royo dates the enclave system in southern Costa Rica to 1941–1984 and then argues for two additional causes: an agrarian structure with severe intrinsic productivity limits (land use, tenure and land capability), and factors external to the territory. Using negative population growth and unmet-basic-needs indices as evidence, it is the most useful corrective for anyone tempted to read the whole social history of the Golfo Dulce hinterland as a single United Fruit story.
verbatim_finding: The so-called Banana Enclave System, present in the south of Costa Rica between 1941 and 1984, has been uniquely and recurringly attributed with the responsibility for the economic underdevelopment of the region.
data_availability: Open-access PDF (Spanish). Analysis is built on Costa Rican census and agrarian-structure indicators (Índice de Desarrollo Social, Necesidades Básicas Insatisfechas, IDA land-distribution records); source data are national statistics, not deposited with the article.
caveat: Note the enclave dates: Royo gives 1941–1984, whereas the Golfito division is usually dated 1938–1985. Canton-level analysis, so it averages over very different communities (Palmar, Sierpe, Puerto Cortés).

title: Global Multi-Resolution Topography synthesis
summary: The methods paper behind GMRT, and the citation that GMRT's own documentation directs users to. It sets out the multi-resolution tiling scheme that preserves the native resolution of swath sonar where it exists and degrades gracefully to compiled global grids where it does not — the mechanism that makes a place like Golfo Dulce look mapped when zoomed out and dissolve into interpolation when zoomed in. Its opening sentence is the honest global statement of the problem this project is about.
verbatim_finding: Seafloor bathymetric data acquired with modern swath echo sounders provide coverage for only a small fraction of the global seabed yet are of high value for studies of the dynamic processes of seafloor volcanism, tectonics, mass wasting, and sediment transport
data_availability: Describes the web services and clients through which the synthesis is distributed; the compilation itself is at marine-geo.org/portals/gmrt. Open access at AGU.
caveat: 2009 methods paper; the synthesis has advanced to v4.5.0 since, so version-specific numbers must come from the GMRT site rather than from here.

title: El cuestionable fundamento legal de la planeada marina en Puerto Jiménez
summary: The legal-planning strand of the marina dispute, written by an environmental lawyer who teaches at both UNA and UCR. Its argument is that the marina rests on the Plan Regulador Parcial Costero de Puerto Jiménez of 2004, which was never submitted to SETENA for environmental viability review, and that Sala Constitucional jurisprudence since 2002 requires an environmental permit for any territorial-planning instrument. It records the constitutionality challenge (expediente 13-003396-0007CO) brought by environmental groups. For a knowledge hub this is the entry point into the Costa Rican land-use-permit machinery that actually decides what gets built on the gulf's shoreline.
verbatim_finding: el proyecto de marina en Puerto Jiménez es que tiene como fundamento un cuestionable plan de ordenamiento territorial denominado Plan Regulador Parcial Costero de Puerto Jiménez
data_availability: None; cites the constitutional-challenge case file and Sala Constitucional votes by number, which are separately retrievable from the Poder Judicial.
caveat: Written in 2013 while the constitutional action was pending; the outcome of expediente 13-003396-0007CO is not covered here and must be checked separately.

title: Shallow gas seeps in the Golfo Dulce, South Pacific of Costa Rica: geological, physicochemical, and biological characterization
summary: The systematic follow-up to Wild et al. (2015) on Golfo Dulce's shallow methane seepage, combining gas composition, water nutrient chemistry, rock petrology, fish and benthic cover censuses and cryptofauna sampling. It quantifies the emissions at 49.5% methane and identifies the host rock as sandstone of the Charco Azul Group, tying the seepage to the regional geology rather than to hydrothermal activity. Ecologically it records 18 fish species and 93 cryptofauna taxa, with a community structure unlike anything else on the Costa Rican Pacific coast, and reports Biffarius ghost shrimp new to the Eastern Tropical Pacific.
verbatim_finding: The seeps are composed of 49.5% methane and the rock that makes up the platform is sandstone from the Charco Azul Group.
data_availability: Gas composition, nutrient concentrations, benthic cover percentages and taxon lists reported within the preprint. Freely readable on Research Square; no separate data deposit found.
caveat: Preprint, version 1 — not peer-reviewed as retrieved. A Spanish-language version of the same work circulates as Moya (2023) via UCR. Check for a journal version before citing numbers.

title: Complejidad estructural de los manglares de Playa Blanca, Escondido y Rincón de Osa, Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The quantitative structural description of three of Golfo Dulce's own mangrove stands, based on transect plots measuring diameter at breast height, basal area, canopy height, stand density and interstitial salinity. Rhizophora racemosa and Pelliciera rhizophorae dominate all three, matching regional expectation, but the striking result is how much the three stands differ from one another: Playa Blanca has the tallest canopy and lowest density, Escondido the densest and shortest canopy and the only Conocarpus erectus. The authors conclude that within-gulf structural variation exceeds the commonalities with regional mangroves — a caution against treating 'the Golfo Dulce mangrove' as a single unit.
verbatim_finding: The dominant species at all three mangroves were Rhizophora racemosa and Pelliciera rhizophorae.
data_availability: Per-site density, basal area, importance values, complexity indices and interstitial-water salinity are tabulated in the open-access article.
caveat: Three stands only, sampled once; the authors note that topographic and historical analysis would be needed to explain the structural differences they document.

title: The abundance of false killer whale, Pseudorca crassidens (Artiodactyla: Delphinidae) in coastal waters of Golfo Dulce and Osa Peninsula, Costa Rica
summary: Fifteen years of opportunistic and systematic cetacean survey data (2001–2015) combined in an open-population POPAN mark–recapture framework to size the false killer whale population using Golfo Dulce, Drake Bay and Caño Island. The result — fewer than 100 individuals, encountered rarely but surviving well — establishes Pseudorca as the most vulnerable of the gulf's regularly occurring odontocetes and supplies the demographic baseline against which increasing vessel traffic and coastal development must be judged.
verbatim_finding: False killer whale abundance in OPW is characterized by a small population size of no more than 100 individuals, complemented by a very low probability of encounter and a contrasting high apparent survival.
data_availability: Photo-identification encounter histories drive the POPAN models; parameter estimates and model selection tables are in the open-access article.
caveat: The authors themselves call the estimate conservative; encounters were largely opportunistic and pooled across a very large study area, so the Golfo Dulce-specific component cannot be separated cleanly.

title: Caracterización físico-química de dos estuarios en la bahía de Golfito, Golfo Dulce, Pacífico de Costa Rica
summary: Eleven monthly cruises through 1998 across 12 stations in two mangrove estuaries of Golfito Bay, measuring salinity, temperature, dissolved oxygen, Secchi depth, suspended matter, dissolved inorganic nutrients and chlorophyll a. It characterises the small-scale, land-facing end of the gulf's hydrography: these estuaries are vertically well mixed rather than stratified, and they carry very high silicate (up to ~980 µmol/L in the rainy season) and strongly seasonal nitrate, with river-station concentrations far exceeding those in the mangrove channel and marine stations. This is the best quantification of the nutrient signal the eastern shore delivers to the gulf, and of its dry/rainy-season contrast.
verbatim_finding: Salinity profiles showed these are vertically mixed or well mixed estuaries, with no anoxic conditions
data_availability: Station-by-station monthly values for all measured variables are tabulated in the article, with dry/rainy season ranges given explicitly. No digital deposit.
caveat: Covers Golfito Bay only — not the Esquinas, Rincón or Coto Colorado inputs, which dominate the gulf's freshwater budget. Spanish text with English abstract; journal DOI does not resolve.

title: Estructura de la población y distribución de Anadara tuberculosa Sowerby (1833) (Mollusca: Bivalvia) en los manglares de Golfito y Playa Blanca de Puerto Jiménez, Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: A three-year (2008–2010) population assessment of the piangua, the mangrove cockle that is the main artisanally harvested invertebrate of the gulf's mangroves. Densities differed twentyfold between Golfito (2.77 ind/m²) and Playa Blanca (0.14 ind/m²), and mean shell length at Golfito (42.1 mm) sits below Costa Rica's 47 mm legal minimum — direct evidence of growth overfishing in the more heavily harvested stand. The paper is the clearest quantitative link in the Golfo Dulce literature between mangrove habitat, a subsistence fishery and a declining stock.
verbatim_finding: These results suggest that A. tuberculosa population is declining in these mangroves.
data_availability: Density, length-frequency, total weight and condition-index data by site and year are tabulated in the open-access article.
caveat: Two mangrove systems only; no independent measure of harvest effort, so the inference that harvesting causes the decline is indirect.

title: Documento para oficialización del Plan de Manejo del Parque Nacional Corcovado
authors: Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación (SINAC)
container: SINAC, Proyecto Planes de Manejo de las ASP de ACOSA
summary: The official management plan for the park that occupies the outer Osa Peninsula and shares a boundary regime with the Golfo Dulce catchment. It matters for the gulf indirectly but concretely: it records the creation and expansion decrees and their elevation to statute, situates the park on the Golfo Dulce topographic sheet, and — through its acronym list and institutional chapter — documents the working constellation around ACOSA (UCR, UNA, TNC, PROMAR, INBio, the Programa de Servicios Ambientales, local NGOs) that any collaboration in the region has to route through.
verbatim_finding: Fue creado por Decreto Ejecutivo Nº 5357-A, publicado en La Gaceta Nº 207 el 31 de octubre de 1975. Posteriormente fue ampliado por el Decreto Ejecutivo No.11148-A, publicado en La Gaceta No. 33 el 15 de febrero de 1980.
data_availability: Boundary decrees, zoning descriptions and programme budgets in the PDF; monitoring data referenced (PROMEC) but not included.
caveat: Dated 2008 and largely superseded in practice; adjacency to Golfo Dulce is contextual — Corcovado's marine frontage is on the open Pacific, not inside the gulf.

title: Propuesta de Plan General de Manejo Integrado de los Refugios de Vida Silvestre: Rio Oro, Pejeperro, Carate, Saimiri, Laguna Azul y Humedal Lacustrino Pejeperrito
authors: Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación (SINAC)
container: SINAC, Área de Conservación Osa, Golfito, Costa Rica
summary: An integrated management plan covering state, mixed and private wildlife refuges around the Osa Peninsula, produced under the German-funded BIOMARCC marine-coastal biodiversity project with the Asociación Costa Rica por Siempre. Beyond the refuges themselves it reproduces the ICT maritime-terrestrial-zone tourism-aptitude declarations for the cantón de Golfito, which is the mechanism by which coastal land around the gulf is opened to or shielded from tourism concessions — including an explicit non-tourist designation for the Coto Colorado mangroves and estuary, the very catchment that carries the oil-palm and rice runoff into Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: Declarar de aptitud no turística los sectores de zona marítimo terrestre aledaña a los manglares y ría del río Coto Colorado, por su vocación agrícola-ganadera
data_availability: Refuge boundaries, threat matrices and the ICT zone declarations are in the PDF. No datasets distributed.
caveat: Covers the Pacific-facing Osa refuges, not the Refugio Nacional de Vida Silvestre Golfito on the gulf itself; no published general management plan for the Golfito refuge could be located on sinac.go.cr.

title: Propuesta de Plan General de Manejo del Parque Nacional Piedras Blancas, 2016 - 2025
authors: Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación (SINAC)
summary: The official management plan for the national park that forms the entire northern shore of Golfo Dulce, and the only such plan that treats a marine strip of the gulf (1 200 ha) as part of a protected area. It sets out the park's Elementos Focales de Manejo — including corals and coral communities, mangroves, the needlefish spawning habitat and the lentic Laguna Machaca — runs an ecological-integrity and threat analysis over each, and produces zoning plus seven management programmes. Its threat chapter is the most explicit official statement linking oil-palm monoculture and eutrophication to degradation inside the protected area, and it flags the absence of an updated baseline for the gulf's corals.
verbatim_finding: En particular la Laguna Machaca, identificada como vacío de conservación por GRUAS II, parece amenazada por un proceso de eutrofización: carece de espejo de agua y está cubierta por plantas acuáticas. Esto se suma a otras presiones como la extracción de recursos, el monocultivo de palma en sus orillas y el pastoreo.
data_availability: Land-tenure tables, zoning areas in hectares and threat-rating matrices are printed in the PDF. GIS layers were produced (SIG advisor Paulo Bermúdez) but are not distributed with the document.
caveat: A 'propuesta' whose stated horizon (2016-2025) has now expired; a successor plan may exist. The sinac.go.cr TLS chain is incomplete, so some clients cannot fetch it even though the file serves fine over curl.

title: Plan General de Manejo de la Reserva Forestal Golfo Dulce 2018 - 2027
authors: Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación (SINAC)
summary: The management plan for the 60 098 ha forest reserve that wraps the western and southern catchment of the gulf and is the main buffer between Corcovado and the shoreline. Its value for a conservation dossier is the land-tenure and governance detail rather than the biology: it breaks the reserve down into Patrimonio Natural del Estado, private title, INDER holdings, untitled occupants, cadastral gaps and the Territorio Indígena Guaymí de Osa, and reports a management-effectiveness score of 42% for 2016 — an unusually frank official admission of weak state capacity in the catchment that drains into Golfo Dulce.
verbatim_finding: La calificación global de la gestión en el periodo de 2016 para la RFGD fue del 42%
data_availability: Land-tenure and zoning tables by hectare and number of parcels are printed in the PDF. Underlying cadastral and GIS layers are not distributed.
caveat: A terrestrial-reserve plan: it does not manage the water column of the gulf. The sinac.go.cr TLS chain is incomplete and some HTTP clients cannot fetch the file.

title: Constraints on inner forearc deformation from balanced cross sections, Fila Costeña thrust belt, Costa Rica
summary: Quantifies deformation on the landward side of Golfo Dulce. Balanced cross sections through the Fila Costeña — the thrust belt that forms the mountain front behind the gulf and shortens the Térraba forearc basin fill — yield a shortening rate of about 40 mm/a, up to half the total Cocos–Panama microplate convergence. The thrust belt is shown to terminate near the Panama border at the onland projection of the subducting Panama Fracture Zone, and its Eocene limestone décollement pinches out away from the Cocos Ridge axis, so the belt's extent maps the subducting ridge. The authors argue shortening is propagating eastward with the migrating Panama triple junction, tying the structural framework around Golfo Dulce directly to the arrival of thickened crust at the trench.
verbatim_finding: we constrain a shortening rate of approximately 40 mm/a and propose that as much as 50% of the total plate convergence rate is taken up in the inner forearc
data_availability: Geologic mapping and two balanced/restored cross sections presented as figures. No deposited dataset. Wiley paywall.
caveat: The ~40 mm/a shortening rate is a maximum derived from one balanced section and depends on assumed timing; Alfaro et al. (2023, 10.1016/j.jsames.2023.104465) propose a revised two-thrust-fault tectonostratigraphy for the Fila Costeña.

title: La población indígena de Costa Rica en el siglo XVI al momento del contacto con los europeos
summary: A revisionist demographic argument that matters for any statement about how many people lived around Golfo Dulce at Spanish contact. Against the figure of ~400,000 that has circulated for three decades, Solórzano defends Bishop Thiel's nineteenth-century estimate of ~27,000 for the territory of modern Costa Rica, reconciling ethnohistorical documents with recent archaeology and with anthropological work on chiefdom scale. Given that the Osa/Golfo Dulce coast was among the most thinly occupied parts of the country, this directly constrains claims about pre-contact population density on the gulf.
verbatim_finding: Durante las últimas tres décadas se ha afirmado que la población indígena de Costa Rica al momento del contacto con los europeos en el siglo XVI ascendía a unos 400 000 habitantes.
data_availability: Open-access PDF, pp. 313–345. Presents population estimates derived from colonial documentary sources and published archaeological survey data; no tabulated dataset is deposited.
caveat: Actively contested. Costa Rican contact-population estimates vary by more than an order of magnitude and this paper argues the low end; cite it as one side of a live debate.

title: Data archive for Anaerobic methane oxidation in a coastal oxygen minimum zone: spatial and temporal dynamics
summary: The most valuable machine-readable dataset currently available for the Golfo Dulce water column: CSV files of methane, nitrite, nitrate and ammonium concentrations, anaerobic methane oxidation rates and rate kinetics, plus reference sequence files, from annual campaigns in January–February 2018, 2019 and 2020. Released CC-BY, it is directly usable for plotting depth profiles of the anoxic layer's nitrogen and methane chemistry without needing the paywalled paper. Version 2 corrects a calculation error in v1 that had underestimated in-situ methane concentrations to roughly a third of their true values.
verbatim_finding: Data collected during annual sampling campaigns to the coastal oxygen minimum zone of Golfo Dulce, carried out in January-February 2018, 2019 and 2020.
data_availability: Open CC-BY download of nutrient_and_methane_concentrations.csv, methane_oxidation_rates.csv, kinetics_of_anaerobic_methane_oxidation.csv, methylococcales.fa and methanofastidiosa.fa via Zenodo and its REST API.
caveat: Registered with a DataCite DOI (10.5281/zenodo.6377988), which is not in Crossref, so it is recorded here by URL. Use version 2 or later — version 1 methane concentrations are wrong by a factor of about three.

title: Anaerobic methane oxidation in a coastal oxygen minimum zone: spatial and temporal dynamics
summary: The strongest modern evidence on both the stability of the redox structure and the methane budget. Three consecutive years of sampling (2018, 2019, 2020) combining biogeochemistry, incubations and 16S rRNA sequencing show a redox zonation that is stable across years, with methane up to 1.7 µmol/L in anoxic bottom waters, yet high anaerobic methane oxidation in the OMZ core (rate constant averaging ~30 /yr in 2018 and ~8 /yr in 2019–2020). OPU3 and Deep Sea-1 Methylococcales clades peak 5–25 m below the oxic–anoxic interface and in the deep anoxic water respectively, implying a microbial filter that suppresses methane escape to the atmosphere.
verbatim_finding: Our results demonstrate a stable redox zonation across the years with high concentrations of methane
data_availability: Full data archive on Zenodo (CC-BY) with methane/nutrient concentrations, oxidation rates, kinetics and reference sequences; 16S amplicon data deposited in sequence archives as stated in the paper.
caveat: Wiley paywall on the article, though the underlying data are open. The three sampling years are all January–February, so seasonal (rainy-season) dynamics are not covered.

title: Fixed-Nitrogen Loss Associated with Sinking Zooplankton Carcasses in a Coastal Oxygen Minimum Zone (Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica)
summary: Shows that the gulf's zooplankton and its anoxic chemistry are coupled in both directions. Using 15N stable-isotope enrichment on carcasses of the gulf's abundant copepods and ostracods exposed to the steep O2 gradient, the authors demonstrate that dead zooplankton sinking through the water column carry their own anoxic microenvironments, hosting dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (up to 30.8 nmol ind−1 d−1), denitrification, anammox and N2O production even where ambient oxygen is present. This extends the Golfo Dulce anammox story (Dalsgaard et al. 2003) from the free water column into particulate biological hotspots, and makes the plankton community a participant in nitrogen loss rather than a passive resident of an OMZ.
verbatim_finding: carcasses of abundant copepods and ostracods provide anoxic microbial hotspots in the pelagic zone by hosting intense anaerobic N-cycle activities even in the presence of ambient O2
data_availability: Rate measurements per individual carcass, depth-integrated pelagic N-loss rates (Table 1) and supplementary material published open access under CC-BY.
caveat: Incubation experiments on collected carcasses; scaling from per-individual rates to whole-basin nitrogen loss depends on carcass abundance estimates that carry large uncertainty.

title: A physical-oceanographic study of Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The definitive physical oceanography of the gulf: field campaigns in 1999 and 2001 by CIMAR-UCR with the University of Bergen, combined with a three-dimensional numerical circulation model. It is the source for how the gulf actually moves water. Because Golfo Dulce sits near the equator, Coriolis is negligible, so cross-gulf structure is set by runoff, local wind and topography rather than rotation; along-gulf temperature and salinity gradients are maintained by the four inner rivers; and the vertical structure differs between the sill (three-layer flow) and the inner basin (two-layer estuarine circulation over near-stagnant deep water). Anyone modelling flushing of the anoxic layer starts here.
verbatim_finding: A three-layer current structure is dominating in the sill area while in the deeper inner part of the gulf a two-layer estuarine circulation takes place above slowly moving deep water.
data_availability: CTD sections, current-meter records and model output are presented as figures. Model setup (Blumberg–Mellor / POM-type) is described but neither the forcing files nor the model output are archived publicly.
caveat: Field data are from two campaigns; the model is not validated against a long current-meter time series. Journal DOI does not resolve — cite by URL.

title: A physical-oceanographic study of Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The most-cited modern statement of the gulf's controlling geometry: an inner basin with a flat bottom at 215 m maximum depth, separated from a shallow outer basin by a sill area 20 km inside the entrance whose effective depth is about 60 m. Critically for our purpose, the paper also shows how thin the bathymetric foundation is under numerical work on this gulf: the Princeton Ocean Model implementation runs on a 66 x 48 cell net at 2 x 2 km resolution, and the authors state only that 'the original bottom matrix is smoothed' — they never cite a source or a survey for that bottom matrix. A 2 km grid cannot resolve a sill that the same paper says is the single control on deep-water renewal.
verbatim_finding: The effective sill depth is about 60 m and prevents water in the inner basin from free exchange with the adjacent coastal water masses.
data_availability: CTD sections, drogue tracks and current-meter records are presented as figures; the model bottom topography appears only as a contour figure (Fig. 11). No grid, no soundings and no bathymetric source are released or named.
caveat: The '60 m effective sill' is an oceanographic inference about exchange, not a surveyed minimum depth over the sill — and it conflicts with the '<30 m' sill quoted in the Spanish literature. The provenance of the model bathymetry is undocumented.

title: A biogeochemical survey of the anoxic basin Golfo Dulce, Costa Rica
summary: The RV Victor Hensen (January 1994) biogeochemical survey that re-occupied Richards' 1969 stations and turned Golfo Dulce into a working laboratory for anoxic-basin biogeochemistry. It quantifies respiration pathways through the water column and sediments, showing oxygen persisting to ~100 m, a pycnocline sitting above the 60 m sill, nitrate-rich water entering at sill depth, and denitrification at anoxic depths. Its key structural conclusion — that the reproduction of the 1969 zonation implies water exchange frequent enough to prevent strongly reducing conditions — is the basis for treating Golfo Dulce as a periodically flushed rather than permanently anoxic basin.
verbatim_finding: Nitrate-rich water entered the bay at sill depth, and denitrification was indicated at anoxic depths.
